atropos.feature_scan

Feature lab: pre-registration-grade scans around atropos.orthogonal.

This module is ANALYTIC TOOLING, not a protocol stage: it produces classification cells and diagnostics that help DESIGN a preregistered run; it never validates a strategy. Every function returns a fixed TypedDict schema (every key present on every outcome, same discipline as atropos.orthogonal, whose orthogonal_check this module re-exports into its pipeline).

The functions, in pipeline order:

  • missingness_scan() -- is missingness random, or does the NaN pattern carry outcome information (selection bias) or correlate with a control (proxy missingness)?
  • correlation_cluster() -- collapses correlated features into clusters and picks one representative per cluster, so the family for Bonferroni is n_effective (clusters), not n_raw (columns).
  • bucket_scan() -- per-feature bucket profile (n, mean, hit rate, normalized mean, bootstrap CI), row-level Spearman monotonicity, permutation p-value, and the Q1/Q2 split that asks WHERE a bucket effect lives (hit rate vs raw outcome vs normalized outcome).
  • interaction_scan() -- 2-D bucket heatmap plus an additive vs full OLS F-test: does the pair interact beyond additivity?
  • rule_fit() -- train/test evaluation of caller-built rules (masks): delta kept-vs-dropped on both splits, honest valid / insufficient_n / unstable statuses.
  • regime_scan() -- per-regime feature profiles against a PREREGISTERED indicator: an unfrozen indicator reads REGIME_UNVERIFIED and can never upgrade a cell to STRONG.
  • threshold_scan() -- a threshold sweep over a parsed (never evaluated) rule template, with the plateau-vs-edge reading that separates a wide ridge from a pick-one-number spike.
  • auto_discovery() -- Bonferroni-gated sweep over an explicit candidate pool; the output is a hypothesis list, EXPLORATORY by construction, never a classification.
  • feature_importance() -- permutation importance for one linear/tree model; a diagnostic that feeds no cell and rescues no PROXY.
  • auto_rule_generation() -- the caller fixes the rule SHAPE, the tool grid-searches values on TRAIN only, and the untouched test split judges the winners; all-fail-on-test reads overfit_warning.

The orchestrator feature_analysis() chains the scans in the order above and classifies every representative feature into one cell::

STRONG              orthogonal pass + monotone + regime pass
                    (verified regime indicator, checkpoint A2)
REGIME_DEPENDENT    orthogonal pass + monotone, regime flips sign
                    (verified indicator, checkpoint A2)
STRONG_UNVERIFIED   orthogonal pass + monotone, no (verified)
                    regime indicator supplied
SHAPE_UNKNOWN       orthogonal pass but monotone fail
PROXY               orthogonal gate fail (incl. collinear with a
                    control -- carries no information beyond it)
NOISE               feature not testable (degenerate column)
EXPLORATORY         auto-discovery output only (checkpoint A3);
                    never assigned to declared features

Recommended actions: build_rule (STRONG), build_rule_with_regime_filter (REGIME_DEPENDENT), prereg_regime_indicator_then_retest (STRONG_UNVERIFIED), investigate_interaction (SHAPE_UNKNOWN), discard (PROXY/NOISE), manual_review_required (EXPLORATORY).

Checkpoint note: this file landed in three verified checkpoints -- A1 (the five defensive/analysis functions + the orchestrator skeleton), A2 (regime_scan + threshold_scan), A3 (auto_discovery, feature_importance, auto_rule_generation -- all EXPLORATORY by construction, this state). The report schema was FROZEN at A1: every key above exists from the first commit. If a future wave wants auto-discovery -> prereg path, that is a separate protocol change, not a tool feature.

Run python -m atropos.feature_scan for a synthetic demo.

   8re-exports into its pipeline).

  16  clusters and picks one representative per cluster, so the family

  21  monotonicity, permutation p-value, and the Q1/Q2 split that asks

  26* :func:`rule_fit` -- train/test evaluation of caller-built rules

  32* :func:`threshold_scan` -- a threshold sweep over a parsed (never

 138# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 139# gates and constants (every number pinned once, named, documented)
 140# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 141_ALPHA = 0.05
 142"""Family-wise alpha behind every p-value gate in this module."""
 143
 144_KS_P_GATE = 0.05
 145"""Missingness: outcome-distribution shift (KS) significance gate."""
 146
 147_NAN_RHO_GATE = 0.3
 148"""Missingness: |pearson| of NaN mask vs control that flags a link."""
 149
 150_MIN_KS_N = 5
 151"""Minimum observations per side before the KS test is allowed."""
 152
 153_MIN_CORR_N = 20
 154"""Minimum rows before a NaN-mask/control correlation is allowed."""
 155
 156_T_Q = 2.0
 157"""Q1/Q2 split significance gate (|t| for means, |z| for hit rates)."""
 158
 159_SPEAR_P_GATE = 0.05
 160"""Row-level Spearman p gate behind every ``monotone`` verdict."""
 161
 162_N_BOOT = 1000
 163"""Bootstrap draws per bucket CI (chunked, memory-bounded)."""
 164
 165_MAX_THRESHOLDS = 7
 166"""Prereg cap on a threshold sweep length (the pick-a-number guard)."""
 167
 168_PLATEAU_SHARE = 0.7
 169"""Edge delta (vs the sweep max) that reads as plateau, not spike."""
 170
 171_EDGE_SHARE = 0.3
 172"""Edge delta (vs the sweep max) below which the sweep reads edge."""
 173
 174_MAX_COMBOS = 200
 175"""Grid-search cap for auto_rule_generation (exploration hygiene)."""
 176
 177_DISCOVERY_NOTE = (
 178    "exploratory -- validation requires prereg + run_full_pipeline"
 179)
 180"""The one-line doctrine every discovery report must carry."""
 181
 182_ALLOWED_OPS = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=")
 183"""The only comparison operators a rule template may use."""
 184
 185_OP_FUNCS = {
 186    "<": np.less,
 187    "<=": np.less_equal,
 188    ">": np.greater,
 189    ">=": np.greater_equal,
 190}

 219class MissingnessEntry(TypedDict):
 220    """Missingness profile of one feature over the union index.
 221
 222    ``ks_p`` compares the outcome distribution where the feature is
 223    NaN against where it is observed (NaN when either side has fewer
 224    than :data:`_MIN_KS_N` observations); ``nan_correlates_with`` maps
 225    every control to the pearson correlation of the NaN indicator
 226    with that control (NaN when under-sampled or the control is
 227    constant); ``warn`` is True only when the fraction exceeds the
 228    caller's threshold AND the pattern is non-random (outcome shift
 229    or control link).
 230    """
 231
 232    nan_fraction: float
 233    ks_p: float
 234    nan_outcome_differs: bool
 235    nan_correlates_with: dict[str, float]
 236    warn: bool
 237
 238
 239class MissingnessReport(TypedDict):
 240    """Per-feature missingness profiles plus the run's notes."""
 241
 242    label: str
 243    nan_threshold: float
 244    features: dict[str, MissingnessEntry]
 245    notes: list[str]
 246
 247
 248class ClusterReport(TypedDict):
 249    """Correlation clusters, representatives and the Bonferroni split.
 250
 251    ``clusters`` holds the member lists (average linkage over
 252    ``1 - |pearson|`` distance, cut at ``threshold``);
 253    ``representatives`` maps EVERY member to its cluster's
 254    representative (the representative maps to itself); the
 255    family-wise Bonferroni threshold is ``alpha / n_effective`` where
 256    ``n_effective`` is the cluster count, not the column count.
 257    """
 258
 259    label: str
 260    threshold: float
 261    clusters: list[list[str]]
 262    representatives: dict[str, str]
 263    n_raw: int
 264    n_effective: int
 265    bonferroni_threshold: float
 266    notes: list[str]
 267

 269class BucketCell(TypedDict):
 270    """Statistics of one bucket: n, outcome mean, hit rate, CI.
 271
 272    ``mean_norm_r`` is the mean of the normalized outcome (the
 273    caller-supplied ``norm_r`` column, defaulting to the outcome
 274    itself); ``ci_lo`` / ``ci_hi`` bound the percentile bootstrap CI
 275    of ``mean_outcome``.
 276    """
 277
 278    n: int
 279    mean_outcome: float
 280    hit_rate: float
 281    mean_norm_r: float
 282    ci_lo: float
 283    ci_hi: float
 284
 285
 286class BucketQSplit(TypedDict):
 287    """Low-half vs high-half bucket comparison (the Q1/Q2 question).
 288
 289    Q1 pools the low bucket indices, Q2 the high ones (an odd middle
 290    bucket is excluded).  ``net_r_t`` / ``norm_r_t`` are Welch t
 291    statistics (Q2 minus Q1), ``hit_rate_z`` the pooled
 292    two-proportion z; each ``*_signal`` flag is True when the stat is
 293    finite and its absolute value reaches :data:`_T_Q`.  When the
 294    caller supplied no ``norm_r`` column, ``norm_r_t`` duplicates
 295    ``net_r_t`` (an affine transform cannot change Welch t) and the
 296    report says so.
 297    """
 298
 299    n_q1: int
 300    n_q2: int
 301    q1_mean: float
 302    q2_mean: float
 303    q1_hit_rate: float
 304    q2_hit_rate: float
 305    q1_norm_r: float
 306    q2_norm_r: float
 307    net_r_t: float
 308    hit_rate_z: float
 309    norm_r_t: float
 310    net_r_signal: bool
 311    hit_rate_signal: bool
 312    norm_r_signal: bool
 313
 314
 315class BucketFeatureReport(TypedDict):
 316    """Full bucket profile of one feature.
 317
 318    ``spearman`` / ``spearman_p`` are the row-level rank correlation
 319    with the outcome; ``p_perm`` is its seeded permutation p-value;
 320    ``monotone`` requires the Spearman gate AND no low-power bucket
 321    (every bucket at least ``min_bucket_n`` rows); ``buckets`` is
 322    ordered by bucket index (low to high).
 323    """
 324
 325    n_buckets_kept: int
 326    spearman: float
 327    spearman_p: float
 328    p_perm: float
 329    monotone: bool
 330    low_power_buckets: list[int]
 331    buckets: list[BucketCell]
 332    q_split: BucketQSplit
 333

 346class InteractionCell(TypedDict):
 347    """One 2-D cell: bucket-a x bucket-b co-occurrence statistics."""
 348
 349    n: int
 350    mean_outcome: float
 351    hit_rate: float
 352
 353
 354class InteractionScanReport(TypedDict):
 355    """Additive-vs-full F-test for one feature pair.
 356
 357    ``cells`` keys are ``"row x col"`` bucket indices; the F-test
 358    compares the additive design (bucket dummies) against the design
 359    plus all dummy products.  ``interaction_present`` is True only
 360    when the F p-value clears :data:`_ALPHA` AND no cell is
 361    under-powered (``min_cell_n``) -- a significant F on starved cells
 362    is not claimed.  ``status`` is ``OK`` or ``INCONCLUSIVE`` (rank
 363    deficient, too few rows, or a degenerate bucket split).
 364    """
 365
 366    label: str
 367    feature_a: str
 368    feature_b: str
 369    n_cells: int
 370    cells: dict[str, InteractionCell]
 371    low_power_cells: list[str]
 372    f_stat: float
 373    p_f: float
 374    interaction_present: bool
 375    status: str
 376    notes: list[str]
 377

 379class RuleFitEntry(TypedDict):
 380    """Train/test evaluation of one caller-built rule mask.
 381
 382    ``delta_*`` is the kept-minus-dropped outcome mean on that split
 383    (NaN when one side is empty); ``stable`` means both deltas are
 384    positive (same sign by construction); ``status`` applies the
 385    sample-size guards first, then the stability verdict.
 386    """
 387
 388    n_train_kept: int
 389    n_test_kept: int
 390    delta_train: float
 391    delta_test: float
 392    stable: bool
 393    status: str
 394
 395
 396class RuleFitReport(TypedDict):
 397    """Rule masks evaluated on a caller-chosen train/test split."""
 398
 399    label: str
 400    rules: dict[str, RuleFitEntry]
 401    best_valid_rule: str | None
 402    notes: list[str]

 414class RegimeScanReport(TypedDict):

 416
 417    ``status`` is ``OK`` only when the indicator carries a
 418    ``prereg_hash``; an unfrozen indicator reads
 419    ``REGIME_UNVERIFIED`` and can never upgrade a cell to STRONG.
 420    ``same_sign[feature]`` is the pairwise sign test across regimes;
 421    ``strongest_regime`` / ``weakest_regime`` name the regimes by
 422    |spearman|.
 423    """

 426    regime_name: str
 427    regime_definition: str
 428    prereg_hash: str | None
 429    status: str

 431    features: dict[str, dict[str, RegimeEntry]]
 432    same_sign: dict[str, bool]
 433    strongest_regime: dict[str, str]
 434    weakest_regime: dict[str, str]
 435    notes: list[str]

 450class ThresholdScanReport(TypedDict):
 451    """Plateau-vs-edge reading of a threshold sweep (checkpoint A2).
 452
 453    ``plateau_detected``: both edge thresholds reach 70% of the best
 454    ``delta_test``; ``edge_detected``: an edge falls below 30% of it
 455    (a spike -- the classic single-threshold overfit signature).
 456    ``optimal_range`` spans the contiguous >= 70%-of-best run around
 457    the argmax, or is ``None`` when no point has a positive delta.
 458    """
 459
 460    label: str
 461    feature: str
 462    op: str
 463    rule_template: str
 464    points: list[ThresholdPoint]
 465    plateau_detected: bool
 466    edge_detected: bool
 467    optimal_range: list[float] | None
 468    notes: list[str]

 502    ci_lo: float

 577# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 578# small helpers shared by the scans
 579# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 580def _validate_fraction(name: str, value: float) -> float:
 581    """Reject a fraction outside the open (0, 1) interval."""
 582    if not np.isfinite(value) or not 0.0 < value < 1.0:
 583        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a float in (0, 1), got {value!r}")
 584    return float(value)
 585
 586
 587def _to_series(values: Any, name: str) -> pd.Series:
 588    """One named float Series view of any 1-D pandas/numpy input."""
 589    return _to_raw_series(values, name).astype(float)
 590
 591
 592def _to_raw_series(values: Any, name: str) -> pd.Series:
 593    """One named Series view of any 1-D input, dtype preserved.
 594
 595    Regime labels may be strings ("trend"/"chop") -- only the scans'
 596    numeric inputs go through the float cast in :func:`_to_series`.
 597    """
 598    frame = frameify(values, name)
 599    if frame.shape[1] != 1:
 600        raise ValueError(
 601            f"input {name!r} must be a single column, got"
 602            f" {frame.shape[1]} columns"
 603        )
 604    series = frame.iloc[:, 0]
 605    series.name = name
 606    return series
 607
 608
 609def _welch_t(first: np.ndarray, second: np.ndarray) -> float:
 610    """Welch t of two samples; t = mean(first) - mean(second).
 611
 612    Fewer than two observations on either side, zero-variance, or a
 613    non-finite denominator returns NaN (no signal, never a fake 0).
 614    """
 615    size_first = float(first.size)
 616    size_second = float(second.size)
 617    if first.size < 2 or second.size < 2:
 618        return float("nan")
 619    var_first = float(np.var(first, ddof=1))
 620    var_second = float(np.var(second, ddof=1))
 621    denom = np.sqrt(var_first / size_first + var_second / size_second)
 622    if not np.isfinite(denom) or denom == 0.0:
 623        return float("nan")
 624    return float((np.mean(first) - np.mean(second)) / denom)
 625
 626
 627def _prop_z(
 628    count_second: float,
 629    size_second: int,
 630    count_first: float,
 631    size_first: int,
 632) -> float:
 633    """Pooled two-proportion z: share(second) minus share(first)."""
 634    if size_first == 0 or size_second == 0:
 635        return float("nan")
 636    pooled = (count_first + count_second) / (size_first + size_second)
 637    if pooled in (0.0, 1.0):
 638        return float("nan")
 639    denom = np.sqrt(
 640        pooled * (1.0 - pooled) * (1.0 / size_first + 1.0 / size_second)
 641    )
 642    if not np.isfinite(denom) or denom == 0.0:
 643        return float("nan")
 644    share_first = count_first / size_first
 645    share_second = count_second / size_second
 646    return float((share_second - share_first) / denom)
 647
 648
 649def _bootstrap_ci(
 650    values: np.ndarray, rng: np.random.Generator
 651) -> tuple[float, float]:
 652    """Percentile bootstrap CI (2.5 / 97.5) of the mean, chunked.
 653
 654    Draws are generated in chunks of 100 so a large bucket cannot
 655    allocate ``(n_boot, n_obs)`` at once.
 656    """
 657    n_obs = values.size
 658    if n_obs == 0:
 659        return float("nan"), float("nan")
 660    means = np.empty(_N_BOOT)
 661    for start in range(0, _N_BOOT, 100):
 662        stop = min(start + 100, _N_BOOT)
 663        draws = rng.choice(values, size=(stop - start, n_obs), replace=True)
 664        means[start:stop] = draws.mean(axis=1)
 665    low, high = np.percentile(means, [2.5, 97.5])
 666    return float(low), float(high)
 667
 668
 669def _spearman_pair(
 670    first: np.ndarray, second: np.ndarray
 671) -> tuple[float, float]:
 672    """Row-level Spearman rho + p; NaN pair for degenerate input."""
 673    if first.size < 3 or np.ptp(first) == 0.0 or np.ptp(second) == 0.0:
 674        return float("nan"), float("nan")
 675    result = stats.spearmanr(first, second)
 676    return float(result.statistic), float(result.pvalue)
 677
 678
 679def _perm_p_spearman(
 680    feature_values: np.ndarray,
 681    outcome_values: np.ndarray,
 682    real_rho: float,
 683    n_perm: int,
 684    rng: np.random.Generator,
 685) -> float:
 686    """Two-sided permutation p of the row-level Spearman rho.
 687
 688    The feature column is shuffled (marginal kept, link broken); the
 689    share of shuffled draws whose |rho| reaches the real |rho| is the
 690    p-value.  Non-finite draw rhos never count as exceeding.
 691    """
 692    exceed = 0
 693    for _ in range(n_perm):
 694        rho_perm = stats.spearmanr(
 695            rng.permutation(feature_values), outcome_values
 696        ).statistic
 697        if np.isfinite(rho_perm) and abs(float(rho_perm)) >= abs(real_rho):
 698            exceed += 1
 699    return exceed / float(n_perm)
 700
 701
 702def _bucket_indices(
 703    values: np.ndarray,
 704    n_buckets: int,
 705    edges: list[float] | None,
 706    notes: list[str],
 707    tag: str,
 708) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:
 709    """Digitize values into buckets from prereg edges or quantiles.
 710
 711    Returns the per-row bucket index (0-based, ``right=False`` bins)
 712    and the number of DISTINCT buckets that survived.  Collapsed
 713    quantile edges shrink the count with a note; empty bins from
 714    explicit edges are kept as honest empty cells.
 715    """
 716    if edges is not None:
 717        interior = np.unique(
 718            np.asarray([float(edge) for edge in edges], dtype=float)
 719        )
 720        source = "edges"
 721    else:
 722        interior = np.unique(
 723            np.quantile(values, np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, n_buckets + 1)[1:-1])
 724        )
 725        source = "quantile edges"
 726    n_kept = int(interior.size) + 1
 727    if edges is None and n_kept < n_buckets:
 728        notes.append(
 729            f"{tag}: only {n_kept} of {n_buckets} buckets distinct"
 730            f" (duplicate {source}); buckets collapsed"
 731        )
 732    return np.digitize(values, interior), n_kept
 733
 734
 735def _hit_rate(values: np.ndarray) -> float:
 736    """Share of strictly positive observations; NaN when empty."""
 737    if values.size == 0:
 738        return float("nan")
 739    return float(np.mean(values > 0.0))
 740
 741
 742def _cell_stats(
 743    outcome_values: np.ndarray,
 744    norm_values: np.ndarray,
 745    rng: np.random.Generator,
 746) -> BucketCell:
 747    """Pack one bucket's n / means / hit rate / bootstrap CI."""
 748    mean_outcome = (
 749        float(np.mean(outcome_values))
 750        if outcome_values.size
 751        else float("nan")
 752    )
 753    mean_norm = (
 754        float(np.mean(norm_values)) if norm_values.size else float("nan")
 755    )
 756    ci_low, ci_high = _bootstrap_ci(outcome_values, rng)
 757    return BucketCell(
 758        n=int(outcome_values.size),
 759        mean_outcome=mean_outcome,
 760        hit_rate=_hit_rate(outcome_values),
 761        mean_norm_r=mean_norm,
 762        ci_lo=ci_low,
 763        ci_hi=ci_high,
 764    )
 765
 766
 767def _q_split(
 768    outcome_values: np.ndarray,
 769    norm_values: np.ndarray,
 770    bucket_ids: np.ndarray,
 771    n_kept: int,
 772) -> BucketQSplit:
 773    """Pool low-half vs high-half buckets and run the three signals.
 774
 775    The low pool takes bucket indices below ``n_kept // 2`` and the
 776    high pool the indices at ``n_kept - n_kept // 2`` and above; an
 777    odd middle bucket is deliberately excluded from both pools.
 778    """
 779    low_ids = range(n_kept // 2)
 780    high_start = n_kept - n_kept // 2
 781    high_ids = range(high_start, n_kept)
 782    mask_q1 = np.isin(bucket_ids, list(low_ids))
 783    mask_q2 = np.isin(bucket_ids, list(high_ids))
 784    out_q1 = outcome_values[mask_q1]
 785    out_q2 = outcome_values[mask_q2]
 786    norm_q1 = norm_values[mask_q1]
 787    norm_q2 = norm_values[mask_q2]
 788    net_t = _welch_t(out_q2, out_q1)
 789    norm_t = _welch_t(norm_q2, norm_q1)
 790    hits_q1 = float(np.sum(out_q1 > 0.0))
 791    hits_q2 = float(np.sum(out_q2 > 0.0))
 792    hit_z = _prop_z(hits_q2, int(out_q2.size), hits_q1, int(out_q1.size))
 793    return BucketQSplit(
 794        n_q1=int(out_q1.size),
 795        n_q2=int(out_q2.size),
 796        q1_mean=float(np.mean(out_q1)) if out_q1.size else float("nan"),
 797        q2_mean=float(np.mean(out_q2)) if out_q2.size else float("nan"),
 798        q1_hit_rate=_hit_rate(out_q1),
 799        q2_hit_rate=_hit_rate(out_q2),
 800        q1_norm_r=float(np.mean(norm_q1)) if norm_q1.size else float("nan"),
 801        q2_norm_r=float(np.mean(norm_q2)) if norm_q2.size else float("nan"),
 802        net_r_t=net_t,
 803        hit_rate_z=hit_z,
 804        norm_r_t=norm_t,
 805        net_r_signal=bool(np.isfinite(net_t) and abs(net_t) >= _T_Q),
 806        hit_rate_signal=bool(np.isfinite(hit_z) and abs(hit_z) >= _T_Q),
 807        norm_r_signal=bool(np.isfinite(norm_t) and abs(norm_t) >= _T_Q),
 808    )
 809
 810
 811# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 812# 1. missingness_scan
 813# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 814def missingness_scan(
 815    outcome: Any,
 816    features: dict[str, Any],
 817    controls: dict[str, Any],
 818    *,
 819    nan_threshold: float = 0.05,
 820    label: str = "unnamed",
 821) -> MissingnessReport:
 822    """Is each feature's missingness random, or does it carry signal?
 823
 824    Works on the UNION index (outer join of outcome, features and
 825    controls) -- the rows that a later inner-join alignment would
 826    silently drop are exactly the rows this scan must judge.  For
 827    every feature: the NaN fraction, a KS test of the outcome where
 828    the feature is NaN vs observed, and the pearson correlation of
 829    the NaN indicator with every control.  ``warn`` is True only when
 830    the fraction exceeds ``nan_threshold`` AND the pattern is
 831    non-random (outcome shift or a control link beyond
 832    :data:`_NAN_RHO_GATE`) -- random missingness never warns.
 833
 834    Args:
 835        outcome: response series (pandas/numpy 1-D array-like).
 836        features: mapping feature name -> single column.
 837        controls: mapping control name -> single column.
 838        nan_threshold: fraction above which a feature's missingness
 839            becomes eligible for the warn flag; in the open (0, 1).
 840        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
 841
 842    Returns:
 843        :class:`MissingnessReport`; every key is present for every
 844        feature, with NaN statistics where a test was under-powered.
 845
 846    Raises:
 847        ValueError: if ``nan_threshold`` is outside (0, 1), an input
 848            is not a single column, or feature/control names collide.
 849
 850    Example::
 851
 852        >>> import numpy as np
 853        >>> import pandas as pd
 854        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
 855        >>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(400)
 856        >>> out = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx)
 857        >>> feat = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx)
 858        >>> feat[out > 1.0] = np.nan
 859        >>> report = missingness_scan(
 860        ...     out, {"feat": feat}, {}, nan_threshold=0.05
 861        ... )
 862        >>> report["features"]["feat"]["nan_outcome_differs"]
 863        True
 864    """
 865    _validate_fraction("nan_threshold", nan_threshold)
 866    feature_names = list(features)
 867    control_names = list(controls)
 868    overlap = sorted(set(feature_names) & set(control_names))
 869    if overlap:
 870        raise ValueError(f"feature and control names collide: {overlap}")
 871    reserved = sorted((set(feature_names) | set(control_names)) & {"outcome"})
 872    if reserved:
 873        raise ValueError(
 874            "the name 'outcome' is reserved for the outcome column;"
 875            f" rename: {reserved}"
 876        )
 877    outcome_series = _to_series(outcome, "outcome")
 878    feature_series = {
 879        name: _to_series(features[name], name) for name in feature_names
 880    }
 881    control_series = {
 882        name: _to_series(controls[name], name) for name in control_names
 883    }
 884    union = pd.concat(
 885        [outcome_series, *feature_series.values(), *control_series.values()],
 886        axis=1,
 887        join="outer",
 888    )
 889    outcome_values = union["outcome"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
 890    entries: dict[str, MissingnessEntry] = {}
 891    notes: list[str] = []
 892    for name in feature_names:
 893        entries[name] = _missingness_entry(
 894            name,
 895            union[name].to_numpy(dtype=float),
 896            outcome_values,
 897            union,
 898            control_names,
 899            nan_threshold=nan_threshold,
 900            notes=notes,
 901        )
 902    return MissingnessReport(
 903        label=label,
 904        nan_threshold=nan_threshold,
 905        features=entries,
 906        notes=notes,
 907    )
 908
 909
 910def _missingness_entry(
 911    name: str,
 912    column: np.ndarray,
 913    outcome_values: np.ndarray,
 914    union: pd.DataFrame,
 915    control_names: list[str],
 916    *,
 917    nan_threshold: float,
 918    notes: list[str],
 919) -> MissingnessEntry:
 920    """Profile one feature's missingness against outcome and controls.
 921
 922    Appends under-power notes to ``notes`` (KS skipped, undersampled
 923    indicator correlations) so no silent NaN reaches the report.
 924    """
 925    nan_mask = np.isnan(column)
 926    nan_fraction = float(np.mean(nan_mask)) if nan_mask.size else 0.0
 927    observed = ~nan_mask & np.isfinite(outcome_values)
 928    missing = nan_mask & np.isfinite(outcome_values)
 929    ks_p = float("nan")
 930    differs = False
 931    if missing.sum() >= _MIN_KS_N and observed.sum() >= _MIN_KS_N:
 932        ks_p = float(
 933            stats.ks_2samp(
 934                outcome_values[missing], outcome_values[observed]
 935            ).pvalue
 936        )
 937        differs = bool(ks_p < _KS_P_GATE)
 938    else:
 939        notes.append(
 940            f"{name}: KS not run (fewer than {_MIN_KS_N} outcome"
 941            " observations on one side)"
 942        )
 943    corr_map: dict[str, float] = {}
 944    mask_used = nan_mask.astype(float)
 945    for control_name in control_names:
 946        control_values = union[control_name].to_numpy(dtype=float)
 947        usable = np.isfinite(control_values)
 948        if (
 949            usable.sum() < _MIN_CORR_N
 950            or np.ptp(control_values[usable]) == 0.0
 951            or np.ptp(mask_used[usable]) == 0.0
 952        ):
 953            # under-sampled, constant control, or no NaN rows at
 954            # all: the indicator correlation is undefined (NaN)
 955            corr_map[control_name] = float("nan")
 956            continue
 957        corr_map[control_name] = float(
 958            stats.pearsonr(
 959                mask_used[usable], control_values[usable]
 960            ).statistic
 961        )
 962    linked = any(
 963        np.isfinite(value) and abs(value) >= _NAN_RHO_GATE
 964        for value in corr_map.values()
 965    )
 966    warn = bool(nan_fraction > nan_threshold and (differs or linked))
 967    return MissingnessEntry(
 968        nan_fraction=nan_fraction,
 969        ks_p=ks_p,
 970        nan_outcome_differs=differs,
 971        nan_correlates_with=corr_map,
 972        warn=warn,
 973    )
 974
 975
 976# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 977# 2. correlation_cluster
 978# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 979def correlation_cluster(
 980    features: dict[str, Any],
 981    outcome: Any,
 982    *,
 983    threshold: float = 0.8,
 984    representatives: dict[str, str] | None = None,
 985    label: str = "unnamed",
 986) -> ClusterReport:
 987    """Cluster correlated features; pick one representative each.
 988
 989    Builds the pearson matrix over the aligned complete rows, converts
 990    it to ``1 - |rho|`` distance and cuts an average-linkage tree at
 991    ``threshold``.  The representative of each cluster is the member
 992    with the largest |pearson| against the outcome (insertion order
 993    breaks ties), unless ``representatives`` explicitly pins the
 994    choice: the mapping ``{member: representative}`` must name the
 995    representative and every OTHER member of its cluster (clusters
 996    with no entry auto-pick), point INTO the same cluster, and never
 997    conflict.  ``bonferroni_threshold`` is
 998    ``alpha / n_effective`` -- the family for downstream gates is the
 999    CLUSTER count, not the raw column count.
1000
1001    Args:
1002        features: mapping feature name -> single column.
1003        outcome: response series; only used to rank representatives.
1004        threshold: cut level of |pearson|; in the open (0, 1).
1005        representatives: optional explicit member -> representative
1006            map (validated strictly, see above).
1007        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
1008
1009    Returns:
1010        :class:`ClusterReport` with clusters in stable insertion
1011        order; every member maps to its representative.
1012
1013    Raises:
1014        ValueError: if ``threshold`` is outside (0, 1), ``features``
1015            is empty, no rows survive alignment, a representative
1016            name is unknown, or the explicit map violates the
1017            every-member-or-none / same-cluster / no-conflict rules.
1018
1019    Example::
1020
1021        >>> import numpy as np
1022        >>> import pandas as pd
1023        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
1024        >>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(200)
1025        >>> base = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(200), index=idx)
1026        >>> twin = 0.9 * base + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(200)
1027        >>> lone = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(200), index=idx)
1028        >>> out = pd.Series(base + 0.3 * rng.standard_normal(200),
1029        ...                 index=idx)
1030        >>> report = correlation_cluster(
1031        ...     {"base": base, "twin": twin, "lone": lone}, out
1032        ... )
1033        >>> report["n_effective"]
1034        2
1035        >>> report["representatives"]["twin"]
1036        'base'
1037    """
1038    checked_threshold = _validate_fraction("threshold", threshold)
1039    if not features:
1040        raise ValueError("features dict must not be empty")
1041    names = list(features)
1042    frames = [
1043        _to_series(outcome, "outcome"),
1044        *(_to_series(features[name], name) for name in names),
1045    ]
1046    aligned = pd.concat(frames, axis=1, join="inner").dropna()
1047    if aligned.empty:
1048        raise ValueError("no rows survive alignment; cannot correlate")
1049    notes: list[str] = []
1050    rho_values = aligned[names].corr().to_numpy(dtype=float)
1051    degenerate = [
1052        name
1053        for position, name in enumerate(names)
1054        if not np.isfinite(rho_values[position, position])
1055    ]
1056    notes.extend(
1057        f"{name}: degenerate column (constant or all-NaN after"
1058        " alignment); treated as uncorrelated"
1059        for name in degenerate
1060    )
1061    rho_values = np.where(np.isfinite(rho_values), rho_values, 0.0)
1062    distance_values = 1.0 - np.abs(rho_values)
1063    np.fill_diagonal(distance_values, 0.0)
1064    distance_values = np.clip(
1065        (distance_values + distance_values.T) / 2.0, 0.0, 1.0
1066    )
1067    if len(names) == 1:
1068        labels = np.array([1])
1069    else:
1070        tree = hierarchy.linkage(
1071            squareform(distance_values, checks=False), method="average"
1072        )
1073        labels = hierarchy.fcluster(
1074            tree, t=1.0 - checked_threshold, criterion="distance"
1075        )
1076    groups: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
1077    for name, cluster_id in zip(names, labels, strict=True):
1078        groups.setdefault(int(cluster_id), []).append(name)
1079    order = sorted(groups, key=lambda key: names.index(groups[key][0]))
1080    clusters = [groups[cluster_id] for cluster_id in order]
1081    outcome_values = aligned["outcome"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
1082    rep_map = _resolve_representatives(
1083        clusters, aligned, outcome_values, representatives or {}
1084    )
1085    n_effective = len(clusters)
1086    return ClusterReport(
1087        label=label,
1088        threshold=checked_threshold,
1089        clusters=clusters,
1090        representatives=rep_map,
1091        n_raw=len(names),
1092        n_effective=n_effective,
1093        bonferroni_threshold=_ALPHA / n_effective,
1094        notes=notes,
1095    )
1096
1097
1098def _resolve_representatives(
1099    clusters: list[list[str]],
1100    aligned: pd.DataFrame,
1101    outcome_values: np.ndarray,
1102    explicit: dict[str, str],
1103) -> dict[str, str]:
1104    """Pick (or validate the caller-pinned) representative per cluster.
1105
1106    Auto rule: the member with the largest |pearson| against the
1107    outcome, insertion order breaking ties.  Explicit rule: the map
1108    must name the representative and every OTHER member of its
1109    cluster, point INTO the same cluster, and never conflict; clusters
1110    with no entry auto-pick.  Every violation raises ValueError.
1111    """
1112    unknown = sorted(set(explicit) - set(aligned.columns) - {"outcome"})
1113    if unknown:
1114        raise ValueError(f"representative map has unknown names: {unknown}")
1115    rep_map: dict[str, str] = {}
1116    for members in clusters:
1117        pinned = [member for member in members if member in explicit]
1118        if pinned:
1119            targets = sorted({explicit[member] for member in pinned})
1120            if len(targets) != 1:
1121                raise ValueError(
1122                    f"cluster {members}: conflicting representatives"
1123                    f" {targets}"
1124                )
1125            chosen = targets[0]
1126            if chosen not in members:
1127                raise ValueError(
1128                    f"cluster {members}: representative {chosen!r} is"
1129                    " not a member of its own cluster"
1130                )
1131            unmapped = sorted(set(members) - {chosen} - set(pinned))
1132            if unmapped:
1133                raise ValueError(
1134                    f"cluster {members}: representatives must name the"
1135                    " representative and every other member; unmapped:"
1136                    f" {unmapped}"
1137                )
1138        else:
1139            chosen = max(
1140                members,
1141                key=lambda member: _outcome_abs_corr(
1142                    aligned, member, outcome_values
1143                ),
1144            )
1145        for member in members:
1146            rep_map[member] = chosen
1147    return rep_map
1148
1149
1150def _outcome_abs_corr(
1151    aligned: pd.DataFrame, member: str, outcome_values: np.ndarray
1152) -> float:
1153    """|pearson| of one member column vs the outcome (-1 for constant).
1154
1155    The -1 floor ranks a degenerate column below any real candidate,
1156    so a constant member can never win the auto-pick.
1157    """
1158    column = aligned[member].to_numpy(dtype=float)
1159    if np.ptp(column) == 0.0:
1160        return -1.0
1161    return abs(float(stats.pearsonr(column, outcome_values).statistic))
1162
1163
1164# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1165# 3. bucket_scan
1166# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1167def bucket_scan(
1168    outcome: Any,
1169    features: dict[str, Any],
1170    *,
1171    n_buckets: int = 5,
1172    bucket_edges: dict[str, list[float]] | None = None,
1173    min_bucket_n: int = 0,
1174    norm_r: Any | None = None,
1175    n_perm: int = 200,
1176    seed: int = 42,
1177    label: str = "unnamed",
1178) -> BucketScanReport:
1179    """Bucket profile, monotonicity and the Q1/Q2 signal split.
1180
1181    For every feature: buckets come from the feature's prereg
1182    ``bucket_edges`` when supplied (else interior quantiles), each
1183    bucket reports n / mean / hit rate / normalized mean / bootstrap
1184    CI, the row-level Spearman gives the monotone verdict (p gate AND
1185    no bucket below ``min_bucket_n``), and a seeded permutation gives
1186    ``p_perm``.  The Q1/Q2 split pools the low and high buckets and
1187    asks where the effect lives: raw outcome (``net_r``), win
1188    frequency (``hit_rate``) or the normalized outcome (``norm_r``).
1189
1190    Args:
1191        outcome: response series.
1192        features: mapping feature name -> single column.
1193        n_buckets: requested bucket count (>= 2).
1194        bucket_edges: optional per-feature interior edges (prereg);
1195            features without an entry fall back to quantiles.
1196        min_bucket_n: power floor per bucket for the monotone
1197            verdict; 0 disables the floor.
1198        norm_r: optional normalized-outcome column (index-aligned
1199            with the outcome; the inner join is performed per
1200            feature); ``None`` uses the outcome itself, in which case
1201            ``norm_r_signal`` mirrors ``net_r_signal`` (Welch t is
1202            invariant to affine scaling -- the report notes this).
1203        n_perm: permutation draws per feature; at least 1.
1204        seed: non-negative seed of the pinned rng.
1205        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
1206
1207    Returns:
1208        :class:`BucketScanReport`; every feature key is present.
1209
1210    Raises:
1211        ValueError: if ``n_buckets`` < 2, ``n_perm`` < 1, ``seed`` is
1212            negative, an input is not a single column, or ``norm_r``
1213            is supplied but does not align with the outcome.
1214
1215    Example::
1216
1217        >>> import numpy as np
1218        >>> import pandas as pd
1219        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
1220        >>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(400)
1221        >>> feat = pd.Series(rng.uniform(0.0, 1.0, 400), index=idx)
1222        >>> out = pd.Series(2.0 * feat + rng.standard_normal(400),
1223        ...                 index=idx)
1224        >>> report = bucket_scan(
1225        ...     out, {"feat": feat}, n_perm=25, seed=42
1226        ... )
1227        >>> report["features"]["feat"]["monotone"]
1228        True
1229    """
1230    validate_int("n_buckets", n_buckets, minimum=2)
1231    validate_int("n_perm", n_perm)
1232    validate_int("seed", seed, minimum=0)
1233    validate_int("min_bucket_n", min_bucket_n, minimum=0)
1234    notes: list[str] = []
1235    outcome_series = _to_series(outcome, "outcome")
1236    norm_is_outcome = norm_r is None
1237    norm_series = (
1238        outcome_series if norm_is_outcome else _to_series(norm_r, "norm_r")
1239    )
1240    entries: dict[str, BucketFeatureReport] = {}
1241    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
1242    for name, feature_value in features.items():
1243        entries[name] = _bucket_profile(
1244            name,
1245            _to_series(feature_value, name),
1246            outcome_series,
1247            norm_series,
1248            n_buckets=n_buckets,
1249            feature_edges=(bucket_edges or {}).get(name),
1250            min_bucket_n=min_bucket_n,
1251            n_perm=n_perm,
1252            rng=rng,
1253            notes=notes,
1254        )
1255    if norm_is_outcome:
1256        notes.append(
1257            "norm_r defaults to the outcome: norm_r_signal mirrors"
1258            " net_r_signal (Welch t is invariant to affine scaling)"
1259        )
1260    return BucketScanReport(
1261        label=label,
1262        n_buckets=n_buckets,
1263        min_bucket_n=min_bucket_n,
1264        norm_r_is_outcome=norm_is_outcome,
1265        features=entries,
1266        notes=notes,
1267    )
1268
1269
1270def _bucket_profile(
1271    name: str,
1272    feature_series: pd.Series,
1273    outcome_series: pd.Series,
1274    norm_series: pd.Series,
1275    *,
1276    n_buckets: int,
1277    feature_edges: list[float] | None,
1278    min_bucket_n: int,
1279    n_perm: int,
1280    rng: np.random.Generator,
1281    notes: list[str],
1282) -> BucketFeatureReport:
1283    """Full bucket profile of one feature (see :func:`bucket_scan`).
1284
1285    Collapsed-quantile notes go to ``notes``; the rng is shared so a
1286    fixed seed reproduces the whole scan bit for bit.
1287    """
1288    aligned_out, aligned_feat, aligned_norm = align_inputs(
1289        outcome_series, feature_series, norm_series
1290    )
1291    rho, rho_p = _spearman_pair(aligned_feat, aligned_out)
1292    bucket_ids, n_kept = _bucket_indices(
1293        aligned_feat, n_buckets, feature_edges, notes, name
1294    )
1295    low_power: list[int] = []
1296    cells: list[BucketCell] = []
1297    for bucket_id in range(n_kept):
1298        mask = bucket_ids == bucket_id
1299        cells.append(_cell_stats(aligned_out[mask], aligned_norm[mask], rng))
1300        if min_bucket_n > 0 and cells[-1]["n"] < min_bucket_n:
1301            low_power.append(bucket_id)
1302    p_perm = (
1303        _perm_p_spearman(aligned_feat, aligned_out, rho, n_perm, rng)
1304        if np.isfinite(rho)
1305        else float("nan")
1306    )
1307    monotone = bool(
1308        np.isfinite(rho)
1309        and np.isfinite(rho_p)
1310        and rho_p <= _SPEAR_P_GATE
1311        and not low_power
1312    )
1313    return BucketFeatureReport(
1314        n_buckets_kept=n_kept,
1315        spearman=rho,
1316        spearman_p=rho_p,
1317        p_perm=p_perm,
1318        monotone=monotone,
1319        low_power_buckets=low_power,
1320        buckets=cells,
1321        q_split=_q_split(aligned_out, aligned_norm, bucket_ids, n_kept),
1322    )
1323
1324
1325# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1326# 4. interaction_scan
1327# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1328def interaction_scan(
1329    outcome: Any,
1330    feature_a: Any,
1331    feature_b: Any,
1332    *,
1333    n_buckets_a: int = 3,
1334    n_buckets_b: int = 4,
1335    min_cell_n: int = 30,
1336    name_a: str = "feature_a",
1337    name_b: str = "feature_b",
1338    label: str = "unnamed",
1339) -> InteractionScanReport:
1340    """Does one pair interact beyond additivity (bucket dummies)?
1341
1342    Quantile-buckets both features, reports the 2-D cell heatmap, then
1343    fits the additive design (intercepts + bucket dummies) and the
1344    full design (plus every dummy product) with OLS and compares them
1345    with the classical nested F-test on the residual sums of squares.
1346    ``interaction_present`` requires the F p-value below
1347    :data:`_ALPHA` AND no cell below ``min_cell_n`` rows -- a
1348    significant F over starved cells is flagged, not claimed.
1349
1350    Args:
1351        outcome: response series.
1352        feature_a: first feature column (heatmap rows).
1353        feature_b: second feature column (heatmap columns).
1354        n_buckets_a: bucket count for ``feature_a`` (>= 2).
1355        n_buckets_b: bucket count for ``feature_b`` (>= 2).
1356        min_cell_n: power floor per cell for the verdict.
1357        name_a: feature name recorded under ``report["feature_a"]``.
1358        name_b: feature name recorded under ``report["feature_b"]``.
1359        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
1360
1361    Returns:
1362        :class:`InteractionScanReport`; ``status`` is ``OK`` or
1363        ``INCONCLUSIVE`` (rank-deficient design, too few rows, or a
1364        degenerate bucket split), with the F statistics NaN in the
1365        latter case.
1366
1367    Raises:
1368        ValueError: if bucket counts are below 2 or an input is not a
1369            single column.
1370
1371    Example::
1372
1373        >>> import numpy as np
1374        >>> import pandas as pd
1375        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
1376        >>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(400)
1377        >>> feat_a = pd.Series(rng.uniform(0, 1, 400), index=idx)
1378        >>> feat_b = pd.Series(rng.uniform(0, 1, 400), index=idx)
1379        >>> out = pd.Series(
1380        ...     feat_a + feat_b + rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx
1381        ... )
1382        >>> report = interaction_scan(out, feat_a, feat_b)
1383        >>> report["interaction_present"]
1384        False
1385    """
1386    validate_int("n_buckets_a", n_buckets_a, minimum=2)
1387    validate_int("n_buckets_b", n_buckets_b, minimum=2)
1388    validate_int("min_cell_n", min_cell_n, minimum=1)
1389    notes: list[str] = []
1390    aligned_out, aligned_a, aligned_b = align_inputs(
1391        _to_series(outcome, "outcome"),
1392        _to_series(feature_a, "feature_a"),
1393        _to_series(feature_b, "feature_b"),
1394    )
1395    ids_a, n_a = _bucket_indices(aligned_a, n_buckets_a, None, notes, name_a)
1396    ids_b, n_b = _bucket_indices(aligned_b, n_buckets_b, None, notes, name_b)
1397    cells: dict[str, InteractionCell] = {}
1398    low_power: list[str] = []
1399    for row_id in range(n_a):
1400        for col_id in range(n_b):
1401            mask = (ids_a == row_id) & (ids_b == col_id)
1402            values = aligned_out[mask]
1403            key = f"{row_id}x{col_id}"
1404            cells[key] = InteractionCell(
1405                n=int(values.size),
1406                mean_outcome=(
1407                    float(np.mean(values)) if values.size else float("nan")
1408                ),
1409                hit_rate=_hit_rate(values),
1410            )
1411            if values.size < min_cell_n:
1412                low_power.append(key)
1413    f_stat, p_f, present, status = _interaction_f_test(
1414        aligned_out,
1415        ids_a,
1416        ids_b,
1417        n_a,
1418        n_b,
1419        low_power=low_power,
1420        notes=notes,
1421    )
1422    if low_power and status == "OK":
1423        notes.append(
1424            f"{len(low_power)} of {len(cells)} cells below min_cell_n"
1425            f" ({min_cell_n}); verdict power-guarded"
1426        )
1427    return InteractionScanReport(
1428        label=label,
1429        feature_a=name_a,
1430        feature_b=name_b,
1431        n_cells=len(cells),
1432        cells=cells,
1433        low_power_cells=low_power,
1434        f_stat=f_stat,
1435        p_f=p_f,
1436        interaction_present=present,
1437        status=status,
1438        notes=notes,
1439    )
1440
1441
1442def _interaction_f_test(
1443    aligned_out: np.ndarray,
1444    ids_a: np.ndarray,
1445    ids_b: np.ndarray,
1446    n_a: int,
1447    n_b: int,
1448    *,
1449    low_power: list[str],
1450    notes: list[str],
1451) -> tuple[float, float, bool, str]:
1452    """Nested OLS F-test: additive bucket design vs full (with products).
1453
1454    Returns ``(f_stat, p_f, present, status)``; every non-testable
1455    branch reads INCONCLUSIVE with a named note, and ``present``
1456    additionally demands no low-power cell.
1457    """
1458    n_rows = int(aligned_out.size)
1459    if n_a < 2 or n_b < 2:
1460        notes.append(
1461            "degenerate bucket split (fewer than 2 distinct buckets on"
1462            " one side); design cannot be built"
1463        )
1464        return float("nan"), float("nan"), False, "INCONCLUSIVE"
1465    if n_rows <= (n_a - 1) + (n_b - 1) + (n_a - 1) * (n_b - 1) + 1:
1466        notes.append(
1467            f"too few rows ({n_rows}) for the full design; F-test is"
1468            " NaN and must not be read as no-interaction"
1469        )
1470        return float("nan"), float("nan"), False, "INCONCLUSIVE"
1471    dummies_a = np.column_stack(
1472        [(ids_a == bucket_id).astype(float) for bucket_id in range(1, n_a)]
1473    )
1474    dummies_b = np.column_stack(
1475        [(ids_b == bucket_id).astype(float) for bucket_id in range(1, n_b)]
1476    )
1477    products = np.column_stack(
1478        [
1479            dummies_a[:, pos_a] * dummies_b[:, pos_b]
1480            for pos_a in range(dummies_a.shape[1])
1481            for pos_b in range(dummies_b.shape[1])
1482        ]
1483    )
1484    ones = np.ones(n_rows)
1485    additive = np.column_stack([ones, dummies_a, dummies_b])
1486    full = np.column_stack([ones, dummies_a, dummies_b, products])
1487    fit_additive = ols_hc0(aligned_out, additive)
1488    fit_full = ols_hc0(aligned_out, full)
1489    if fit_full["rank_deficient"] or fit_additive["rank_deficient"]:
1490        notes.append(
1491            "design rank-deficient; F-test is NaN and must not be"
1492            " read as no-interaction"
1493        )
1494        return float("nan"), float("nan"), False, "INCONCLUSIVE"
1495    rss_additive = float(
1496        np.sum((aligned_out - additive @ fit_additive["beta"]) ** 2)
1497    )
1498    rss_full = float(np.sum((aligned_out - full @ fit_full["beta"]) ** 2))
1499    df_full = n_rows - full.shape[1]
1500    df_diff = int(full.shape[1] - additive.shape[1])
1501    if df_full <= 0 or df_diff <= 0 or rss_full <= 0.0:
1502        notes.append("degenerate residual sums; F-test is NaN")
1503        return float("nan"), float("nan"), False, "INCONCLUSIVE"
1504    f_stat = ((rss_additive - rss_full) / df_diff) / (rss_full / df_full)
1505    p_f = float(stats.f.sf(f_stat, df_diff, df_full))
1506    present = bool(np.isfinite(p_f) and p_f < _ALPHA and not low_power)
1507    if low_power and np.isfinite(p_f) and p_f < _ALPHA:
1508        notes.append(
1509            "F significant but low_power_cells present;"
1510            " interaction_present stays False (power guard)"
1511        )
1512    return f_stat, p_f, present, "OK"
1513
1514
1515# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1516# 5. rule_fit
1517# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1518def rule_fit(
1519    outcome: Any,
1520    rules: dict[str, Any],
1521    *,
1522    train_idx: Any,
1523    test_idx: Any,
1524    min_n_train: int = 100,
1525    min_n_test: int = 50,
1526    label: str = "unnamed",
1527) -> RuleFitReport:
1528    """Evaluate caller-built rule masks on a frozen train/test split.
1529
1530    For every rule (a boolean mask over the outcome positions) the
1531    kept-minus-dropped outcome mean is computed on the train indices
1532    and on the test indices.  ``status`` applies the sample-size
1533    guards first (``insufficient_n``), then reads the deltas: both
1534    positive -> ``valid``, anything else -> ``unstable`` (a rule that
1535    works on train but not on test lands here -- the honest overfit
1536    signature).  ``best_valid_rule`` names the valid rule with the
1537    largest ``delta_test``, or ``None`` when no rule is valid.
1538
1539    Args:
1540        outcome: response series WITHOUT NaN (NaN rows would corrupt
1541            the positional mask semantics; align and drop first).
1542        rules: mapping rule name -> boolean mask (Series or array)
1543            over the outcome positions.
1544        train_idx: positional indices of the train split.
1545        test_idx: positional indices of the test split; must not
1546            overlap ``train_idx``.
1547        min_n_train: minimum kept rows on train for ``valid``.
1548        min_n_test: minimum kept rows on test for ``valid``.
1549        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
1550
1551    Returns:
1552        :class:`RuleFitReport` with one entry per rule.
1553
1554    Raises:
1555        ValueError: if ``outcome`` contains NaN, the splits are empty
1556            or overlapping, an index is out of range, a mask's length
1557            differs from the outcome, or ``rules`` is empty.
1558
1559    Example::
1560
1561        >>> import numpy as np
1562        >>> import pandas as pd
1563        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
1564        >>> rows = np.arange(300)
1565        >>> out = pd.Series(
1566        ...     np.where(rows % 2 == 0, -1.0, 1.0)
1567        ...     + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(300)
1568        ... )
1569        >>> rule = rows % 2 == 0
1570        >>> report = rule_fit(
1571        ...     out, {"parity": rule},
1572        ...     train_idx=np.arange(200), test_idx=np.arange(200, 300),
1573        ...     min_n_train=10, min_n_test=5,
1574        ... )
1575        >>> report["rules"]["parity"]["status"]
1576        'unstable'
1577    """
1578    validate_int("min_n_train", min_n_train, minimum=1)
1579    validate_int("min_n_test", min_n_test, minimum=1)
1580    if not rules:
1581        raise ValueError("rules dict must not be empty")
1582    outcome_series = _to_series(outcome, "outcome")
1583    if bool(outcome_series.isna().any()):
1584        raise ValueError(
1585            "outcome contains NaN; align and drop rows before rule_fit"
1586        )
1587    outcome_values = outcome_series.to_numpy(dtype=float)
1588    train_positions = np.asarray(train_idx, dtype=int).reshape(-1)
1589    test_positions = np.asarray(test_idx, dtype=int).reshape(-1)
1590    if train_positions.size == 0 or test_positions.size == 0:
1591        raise ValueError("train_idx and test_idx must both be non-empty")
1592    if set(train_positions.tolist()) & set(test_positions.tolist()):
1593        raise ValueError("train_idx and test_idx overlap")
1594    total = outcome_values.size
1595    splits = (
1596        ("train_idx", train_positions),
1597        ("test_idx", test_positions),
1598    )
1599    for tag, positions in splits:
1600        if positions.min() < 0 or positions.max() >= total:
1601            raise ValueError(
1602                f"{tag} out of range for outcome of {total} rows"
1603            )
1604    entries: dict[str, RuleFitEntry] = {}
1605    notes: list[str] = []
1606    for name, mask_value in rules.items():
1607        entries[name] = _rule_entry(
1608            name,
1609            mask_value,
1610            outcome_values,
1611            train_positions,
1612            test_positions,
1613            min_n_train=min_n_train,
1614            min_n_test=min_n_test,
1615            notes=notes,
1616        )
1617    valid_names = [
1618        name
1619        for name, entry in entries.items()
1620        if entry["status"] == _STATUS_VALID
1621    ]
1622    best_valid: str | None = None
1623    if valid_names:
1624        best_valid = max(
1625            valid_names, key=lambda name: entries[name]["delta_test"]
1626        )
1627    return RuleFitReport(
1628        label=label,
1629        rules=entries,
1630        best_valid_rule=best_valid,
1631        notes=notes,
1632    )
1633
1634
1635def _rule_entry(
1636    name: str,
1637    mask_value: Any,
1638    outcome_values: np.ndarray,
1639    train_positions: np.ndarray,
1640    test_positions: np.ndarray,
1641    *,
1642    min_n_train: int,
1643    min_n_test: int,
1644    notes: list[str],
1645) -> RuleFitEntry:
1646    """Evaluate one rule mask on the frozen split (see :func:`rule_fit`).
1647
1648    Empty split sides read NaN deltas with an explicit note; the
1649    status ladder is n-guard first, then the both-deltas-positive
1650    stability verdict.
1651    """
1652    total = outcome_values.size
1653    mask = np.asarray(mask_value, dtype=bool).reshape(-1)
1654    if mask.size != total:
1655        raise ValueError(
1656            f"rule {name!r}: mask length {mask.size} != outcome"
1657            f" length {total}"
1658        )
1659    kept_train = outcome_values[train_positions][mask[train_positions]]
1660    drop_train = outcome_values[train_positions][~mask[train_positions]]
1661    kept_test = outcome_values[test_positions][mask[test_positions]]
1662    drop_test = outcome_values[test_positions][~mask[test_positions]]
1663    delta_train = (
1664        float(np.mean(kept_train) - np.mean(drop_train))
1665        if kept_train.size and drop_train.size
1666        else float("nan")
1667    )
1668    delta_test = (
1669        float(np.mean(kept_test) - np.mean(drop_test))
1670        if kept_test.size and drop_test.size
1671        else float("nan")
1672    )
1673    n_train_kept = int(kept_train.size)
1674    n_test_kept = int(kept_test.size)
1675    stable = bool(
1676        np.isfinite(delta_train)
1677        and np.isfinite(delta_test)
1678        and delta_train > 0.0
1679        and delta_test > 0.0
1680    )
1681    if not (np.isfinite(delta_train) and np.isfinite(delta_test)):
1682        status = _STATUS_INSUFFICIENT
1683        notes.append(
1684            f"rule {name!r}: one split side is empty; deltas are NaN"
1685        )
1686    elif n_train_kept < min_n_train or n_test_kept < min_n_test:
1687        status = _STATUS_INSUFFICIENT
1688    elif stable:
1689        status = _STATUS_VALID
1690    else:
1691        status = _STATUS_UNSTABLE
1692    return RuleFitEntry(
1693        n_train_kept=n_train_kept,
1694        n_test_kept=n_test_kept,
1695        delta_train=delta_train,
1696        delta_test=delta_test,
1697        stable=stable,
1698        status=status,
1699    )
1700
1701
1702# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1703# 6. regime_scan (checkpoint A2)
1704# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1705def regime_scan(
1706    outcome: Any,
1707    features: dict[str, Any],
1708    regime_indicator: dict[str, Any],
1709    *,
1710    min_regime_n: int = 100,
1711    label: str = "unnamed",
1712) -> RegimeScanReport:
1713    """Is a feature's effect regime-stable, or does the sign flip?
1714
1715    Splits the aligned sample by the caller's regime indicator (a
1716    dict carrying ``name``, ``definition``, ``prereg_hash`` and the
1717    ``values`` Series) and profiles every feature inside every regime
1718    value: n, row-level Spearman, and the monotone verdict.  The
1719    indicator MUST be preregistered (``prereg_hash``): an unfrozen
1720    indicator reads ``REGIME_UNVERIFIED`` -- cells are computed but
1721    can never upgrade a classification to STRONG.  Regimes with fewer
1722    than ``min_regime_n`` rows are excluded from the sign comparison
1723    with a note.
1724
1725    Args:
1726        outcome: response series.
1727        features: mapping feature name -> single column.
1728        regime_indicator: ``{name, definition, prereg_hash, values}``;
1729            ``values`` is the regime Series (labels may be numeric or
1730            string), index-aligned with the outcome.
1731        min_regime_n: minimum rows for a regime to qualify for the
1732            sign comparison; at least 1.
1733        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
1734
1735    Returns:
1736        :class:`RegimeScanReport`; ``same_sign[feature]`` is the
1737        pairwise sign test over qualifying regimes, ``strongest_regime``
1738        / ``weakest_regime`` name the regimes by |spearman|.
1739
1740    Raises:
1741        ValueError: if the indicator dict misses a key, has an empty
1742            name/definition, ``min_regime_n`` < 1, or an input is not
1743            a single column.
1744
1745    Example::
1746
1747        >>> import numpy as np
1748        >>> import pandas as pd
1749        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
1750        >>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(400)
1751        >>> feat = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx)
1752        >>> out = pd.Series(2.0 * feat + rng.standard_normal(400),
1753        ...                 index=idx)
1754        >>> regime = pd.Series(np.where(rng.random(400) < 0.5, 0, 1),
1755        ...                    index=idx)
1756        >>> report = regime_scan(
1757        ...     out, {"feat": feat},
1758        ...     {"name": "coin", "definition": "independent coin",
1759        ...      "prereg_hash": "hash", "values": regime},
1760        ...     min_regime_n=50,
1761        ... )
1762        >>> report["same_sign"]["feat"]
1763        True
1764    """
1765    for key in ("name", "definition", "prereg_hash", "values"):
1766        if key not in regime_indicator:
1767            raise ValueError(
1768                f"regime_indicator must carry {key!r}; got keys"
1769                f" {sorted(regime_indicator)}"
1770            )
1771    if not regime_indicator["name"] or not regime_indicator["definition"]:
1772        raise ValueError(
1773            "regime_indicator name and definition must be non-empty"
1774        )
1775    validate_int("min_regime_n", min_regime_n, minimum=1)
1776    prereg_hash = regime_indicator["prereg_hash"]
1777    notes: list[str] = []
1778    if prereg_hash:
1779        status = "OK"
1780    else:
1781        status = "REGIME_UNVERIFIED"
1782        notes.append(
1783            "regime indicator carries no prereg_hash: status"
1784            " REGIME_UNVERIFIED -- cells can never upgrade a"
1785            " classification to STRONG"
1786        )
1787    outcome_series = _to_series(outcome, "outcome")
1788    values_series = _to_raw_series(regime_indicator["values"], "regime_value")
1789    entries: dict[str, dict[str, RegimeEntry]] = {}
1790    same_sign: dict[str, bool] = {}
1791    strongest_regime: dict[str, str] = {}
1792    weakest_regime: dict[str, str] = {}
1793    for name, feature_value in features.items():
1794        feature_series = _to_series(feature_value, name)
1795        frame = pd.concat(
1796            [outcome_series, feature_series, values_series],
1797            axis=1,
1798            join="inner",
1799        ).dropna()
1800        aligned_out = frame["outcome"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
1801        aligned_feat = frame[name].to_numpy(dtype=float)
1802        labels = frame["regime_value"].to_numpy()
1803        feature_entries: dict[str, RegimeEntry] = {}
1804        for label_value in sorted(set(labels.tolist()), key=str):
1805            mask = labels == label_value
1806            slice_rho, slice_p = _spearman_pair(
1807                aligned_feat[mask], aligned_out[mask]
1808            )
1809            feature_entries[str(label_value)] = RegimeEntry(
1810                n=int(mask.sum()),
1811                spearman=slice_rho,
1812                spearman_p=slice_p,
1813                monotone=bool(
1814                    np.isfinite(slice_rho)
1815                    and np.isfinite(slice_p)
1816                    and slice_p <= _SPEAR_P_GATE
1817                ),
1818            )
1819        qualifying = [
1820            regime_key
1821            for regime_key, entry in feature_entries.items()
1822            if entry["n"] >= min_regime_n
1823        ]
1824        excluded = [
1825            regime_key
1826            for regime_key, entry in feature_entries.items()
1827            if entry["n"] < min_regime_n
1828        ]
1829        if excluded:
1830            notes.append(
1831                f"{name}: regimes excluded from the sign comparison"
1832                f" (below min_regime_n = {min_regime_n}): {excluded}"
1833            )
1834        if len(qualifying) < 2:
1835            notes.append(
1836                f"{name}: fewer than 2 qualifying regimes; same_sign"
1837                " reads False (not testable, not a flip)"
1838            )
1839            same_sign[name] = False
1840            strongest_regime[name] = ""
1841            weakest_regime[name] = ""
1842        else:
1843            rhos = {
1844                regime_key: feature_entries[regime_key]["spearman"]
1845                for regime_key in qualifying
1846            }
1847            signs = {
1848                np.sign(value)
1849                for value in rhos.values()
1850                if np.isfinite(value)
1851            }
1852            same_sign[name] = bool(len(signs) == 1 and signs)
1853            strongest_regime[name] = max(
1854                qualifying, key=lambda key: abs(rhos[key])
1855            )
1856            weakest_regime[name] = min(
1857                qualifying, key=lambda key: abs(rhos[key])
1858            )
1859        entries[name] = feature_entries
1860    return RegimeScanReport(
1861        label=label,
1862        regime_name=str(regime_indicator["name"]),
1863        regime_definition=str(regime_indicator["definition"]),
1864        prereg_hash=prereg_hash if prereg_hash else None,
1865        status=status,
1866        min_regime_n=min_regime_n,
1867        features=entries,
1868        same_sign=same_sign,
1869        strongest_regime=strongest_regime,
1870        weakest_regime=weakest_regime,
1871        notes=notes,
1872    )
1873
1874
1875# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1876# 7. threshold_scan (checkpoint A2)
1877# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1878def _parse_rule_template(
1879    rule_template: str, feature_name: str
1880) -> tuple[str, Any]:
1881    """Parse ``"<feature> <op> {t}"`` without ever evaluating a string.
1882
1883    Returns the comparison operator's numpy function and the rule's
1884    feature token.  Every deviation (missing ``{t}``, unknown
1885    operator, feature token mismatch) raises ValueError -- a template
1886    is parsed, never ``eval``-ed.
1887    """
1888    if "{t}" not in rule_template:
1889        raise ValueError(
1890            f"rule_template must contain the {{t}} placeholder:"
1891            f" {rule_template!r}"
1892        )
1893    prefix_tokens = rule_template.partition("{t}")[0].split()
1894    if len(prefix_tokens) < 2:
1895        raise ValueError(
1896            "rule_template must read '<feature> <op> {t}':"
1897            f" {rule_template!r}"
1898        )
1899    op = prefix_tokens[-1]
1900    feature_token = prefix_tokens[-2]
1901    if op not in _ALLOWED_OPS:
1902        raise ValueError(
1903            f"rule_template operator must be one of {list(_ALLOWED_OPS)},"
1904            f" got {op!r}"
1905        )
1906    if feature_token != feature_name:
1907        raise ValueError(
1908            f"rule_template names feature {feature_token!r} but the"
1909            f" supplied feature is {feature_name!r}"
1910        )
1911    return op, _OP_FUNCS[op]
1912
1913
1914def threshold_scan(
1915    outcome: Any,
1916    feature: Any,
1917    rule_template: str,
1918    threshold_values: list[float],
1919    *,
1920    feature_name: str,
1921    train_idx: Any,
1922    test_idx: Any,
1923    min_n_kept: int = 100,
1924    label: str = "unnamed",
1925) -> ThresholdScanReport:
1926    """Sweep one threshold over a fixed rule shape, train then test.
1927
1928    The template pins the shape (``"<feature> <op> {t}"``, parsed,
1929    never evaluated); each threshold builds the rule mask on the
1930    aligned sample and reuses the :func:`rule_fit` ladder
1931    (``min_n_kept`` floors both splits).  The sweep-level reading:
1932    ``plateau_detected`` when both edge deltas hold
1933    :data:`_PLATEAU_SHARE` of the best ``delta_test`` (a wide ridge,
1934    safe to ship), ``edge_detected`` when an edge falls below
1935    :data:`_EDGE_SHARE` of it (a spike -- the pick-one-number
1936    overfit signature), and ``optimal_range`` the contiguous
1937    >= share run around the argmax.
1938
1939    Args:
1940        outcome: response series WITHOUT NaN (aligned with feature).
1941        feature: the feature column the template compares against.
1942        rule_template: format string ``"<feature> <op> {t}"``.
1943        threshold_values: the preregistered thresholds; at most
1944            :data:`_MAX_THRESHOLDS`, at least 2.
1945        feature_name: the feature's declared name (validated against
1946            the template's feature token).
1947        train_idx: positional train split.
1948        test_idx: positional test split (must not overlap train).
1949        min_n_kept: minimum kept rows per split for ``valid``.
1950        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
1951
1952    Returns:
1953        :class:`ThresholdScanReport` with one point per threshold.
1954
1955    Raises:
1956        ValueError: on template deviations (see
1957            :func:`_parse_rule_template`), a sweep outside
1958            [2, _MAX_THRESHOLDS], NaN outcome, or bad splits (the
1959            :func:`rule_fit` guards).
1960
1961    Example::
1962
1963        >>> import numpy as np
1964        >>> import pandas as pd
1965        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
1966        >>> rows = np.arange(600)
1967        >>> feat = pd.Series(rng.uniform(0, 1, 600), index=rows)
1968        >>> out = pd.Series(
1969        ...     np.where(feat < 0.65, 1.0, 0.0)
1970        ...     + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(600), index=rows
1971        ... )
1972        >>> report = threshold_scan(
1973        ...     out, feat, "feat < {t}",
1974        ...     [0.7, 0.75, 0.8, 0.85, 0.9],
1975        ...     feature_name="feat",
1976        ...     train_idx=np.arange(400), test_idx=np.arange(400, 600),
1977        ...     min_n_kept=30,
1978        ... )
1979        >>> report["plateau_detected"], report["edge_detected"]
1980        (True, False)
1981    """
1982    op, op_func = _parse_rule_template(rule_template, feature_name)
1983    if len(threshold_values) > _MAX_THRESHOLDS:
1984        raise ValueError(
1985            f"threshold sweep length {len(threshold_values)} exceeds"
1986            f" the prereg cap {_MAX_THRESHOLDS}; freeze fewer values"
1987        )
1988    if len(threshold_values) < 2:
1989        raise ValueError(
1990            "threshold sweep needs at least 2 values to read plateau/edge"
1991        )
1992    validate_int("min_n_kept", min_n_kept, minimum=1)
1993    notes: list[str] = []
1994    outcome_series = _to_series(outcome, "outcome")
1995    feature_series = _to_series(feature, feature_name)
1996    frame = pd.concat(
1997        [outcome_series, feature_series], axis=1, join="inner"
1998    ).dropna()
1999    aligned_out = frame["outcome"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
2000    aligned_feat = frame[feature_name].to_numpy(dtype=float)
2001    train_positions = np.asarray(train_idx, dtype=int).reshape(-1)
2002    test_positions = np.asarray(test_idx, dtype=int).reshape(-1)
2003    points: list[ThresholdPoint] = []
2004    for value in threshold_values:
2005        mask = op_func(aligned_feat, float(value))
2006        rule_str = rule_template.format(t=repr(float(value)))
2007        entry = _rule_entry(
2008            rule_str,
2009            mask,
2010            aligned_out,
2011            train_positions,
2012            test_positions,
2013            min_n_train=min_n_kept,
2014            min_n_test=min_n_kept,
2015            notes=notes,
2016        )
2017        points.append(
2018            ThresholdPoint(
2019                threshold=float(value),
2020                rule_str=rule_str,
2021                n_train_kept=entry["n_train_kept"],
2022                n_test_kept=entry["n_test_kept"],
2023                delta_train=entry["delta_train"],
2024                delta_test=entry["delta_test"],
2025                status=entry["status"],
2026            )
2027        )
2028    finite_deltas = [
2029        point["delta_test"]
2030        for point in points
2031        if np.isfinite(point["delta_test"])
2032    ]
2033    plateau = False
2034    edge = False
2035    optimal_range: list[float] | None = None
2036    if len(finite_deltas) < 2:
2037        notes.append(
2038            "fewer than 2 points have a finite delta_test;"
2039            " plateau/edge read False (not testable)"
2040        )
2041    else:
2042        max_delta = max(finite_deltas)
2043        if max_delta <= 0:
2044            notes.append(
2045                "no positive delta_test on the sweep; plateau/edge"
2046                " read False (the rule shape itself fails on test)"
2047            )
2048        else:
2049            first_delta = finite_deltas[0]
2050            last_delta = finite_deltas[-1]
2051            plateau = bool(
2052                first_delta >= _PLATEAU_SHARE * max_delta
2053                and last_delta >= _PLATEAU_SHARE * max_delta
2054            )
2055            edge = bool(
2056                first_delta < _EDGE_SHARE * max_delta
2057                or last_delta < _EDGE_SHARE * max_delta
2058            )
2059            best_pos = finite_deltas.index(max_delta)
2060            low_pos = best_pos
2061            while (
2062                low_pos > 0
2063                and finite_deltas[low_pos - 1] >= _PLATEAU_SHARE * max_delta
2064            ):
2065                low_pos -= 1
2066            high_pos = best_pos
2067            while (
2068                high_pos < len(finite_deltas) - 1
2069                and finite_deltas[high_pos + 1] >= _PLATEAU_SHARE * max_delta
2070            ):
2071                high_pos += 1
2072            finite_points = [
2073                point for point in points if np.isfinite(point["delta_test"])
2074            ]
2075            optimal_range = [
2076                finite_points[low_pos]["threshold"],
2077                finite_points[high_pos]["threshold"],
2078            ]
2079    return ThresholdScanReport(
2080        label=label,
2081        feature=feature_name,
2082        op=op,
2083        rule_template=rule_template,
2084        points=points,
2085        plateau_detected=plateau,
2086        edge_detected=edge,
2087        optimal_range=optimal_range,
2088        notes=notes,
2089    )
2090
2091
2092# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
2093# 8. auto_discovery (checkpoint A3; EXPLORATORY by construction)
2094# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
2095def auto_discovery(
2096    outcome: Any,
2097    candidate_pool: dict[str, Any],
2098    controls: dict[str, Any],
2099    *,
2100    max_features: int = 20,
2101    min_abs_spearman: float = 0.15,
2102    orthogonal_threshold: float | None = None,
2103    label: str = "unnamed",
2104) -> DiscoveryReport:
2105    """Sweep a candidate pool for effects; the output is a HYPOTHESIS list.
2106
2107    Every candidate that clears the Bonferroni t-gate (derived from
2108    the number of TESTED candidates: ``alpha / n_tested`` two-sided
2109    normal quantile) and a light spearman pre-filter is listed with
2110    its t, its monotone flag and its Bonferroni-adjusted p.  The
2111    report is EXPLORATORY by construction: it never assigns cells,
2112    never names a best feature, and its doctrine note requires
2113    preregistration + the full pipeline before any candidate can be
2114    believed.  Candidates whose |spearman| against the outcome is
2115    below ``min_abs_spearman`` are not tested (and shrink the
2116    Bonferroni family accordingly, with a note).
2117
2118    Args:
2119        outcome: response series.
2120        candidate_pool: EXPLICIT mapping candidate name -> single
2121            column (an auto-scrape of a frame is deliberately not
2122            supported; the caller owns the pool).
2123        controls: mapping control name -> single column (same rules).
2124        max_features: pool-size cap (exploration hygiene); a larger
2125            pool raises.
2126        min_abs_spearman: pre-filter floor on |spearman| vs the
2127            outcome; 0 disables the filter.
2128        orthogonal_threshold: explicit |t| gate; ``None`` derives the
2129            Bonferroni gate from ``alpha / n_tested``.
2130        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
2131
2132    Returns:
2133        :class:`DiscoveryReport` with ``note`` fixed to
2134        :data:`_DISCOVERY_NOTE`.
2135
2136    Raises:
2137        ValueError: if the pool exceeds ``max_features``, is empty,
2138            ``min_abs_spearman`` is negative, a control collides with
2139            a candidate name, or an input is not a single column.
2140
2141    Example::
2142
2143        >>> import numpy as np
2144        >>> import pandas as pd
2145        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
2146        >>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(500)
2147        >>> planted = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(500), index=idx)
2148        >>> null = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(500), index=idx)
2149        >>> out = pd.Series(1.5 * planted + rng.standard_normal(500),
2150        ...                 index=idx)
2151        >>> report = auto_discovery(
2152        ...     out, {"planted": planted, "null": null}, {},
2153        ...     max_features=5, min_abs_spearman=0.0,
2154        ... )
2155        >>> [entry["feature"] for entry in report["discovered"]]
2156        ['planted']
2157        >>> report["all_below_threshold"]
2158        False
2159    """
2160    if not candidate_pool:
2161        raise ValueError("candidate_pool must not be empty")
2162    if len(candidate_pool) > max_features:
2163        raise ValueError(
2164            f"candidate pool size {len(candidate_pool)} exceeds"
2165            f" max_features ({max_features}); the caller must shrink"
2166            " the pool explicitly"
2167        )
2168    if min_abs_spearman < 0.0 or not np.isfinite(min_abs_spearman):
2169        raise ValueError(
2170            f"min_abs_spearman must be a finite float >= 0, got"
2171            f" {min_abs_spearman!r}"
2172        )
2173    candidate_names = list(candidate_pool)
2174    control_names = list(controls)
2175    overlap = sorted(set(candidate_names) & set(control_names))
2176    if overlap:
2177        raise ValueError(f"candidate and control names collide: {overlap}")
2178    outcome_series = _to_series(outcome, "outcome")
2179    control_series = [
2180        _to_series(controls[name], name) for name in control_names
2181    ]
2182    notes: list[str] = []
2183    tested: dict[str, pd.Series] = {}
2184    for name in candidate_names:
2185        candidate_series = _to_series(candidate_pool[name], name)
2186        aligned_out, aligned_feat = align_inputs(
2187            outcome_series, candidate_series
2188        )
2189        rho, rho_p = _spearman_pair(aligned_feat, aligned_out)
2190        if (
2191            min_abs_spearman > 0.0
2192            and np.isfinite(rho)
2193            and abs(rho) < min_abs_spearman
2194        ):
2195            notes.append(
