def auto_discovery( outcome: Any, candidate_pool: dict[str, typing.Any], controls: dict[str, typing.Any], *, max_features: int = 20, min_abs_spearman: float = 0.15, orthogonal_threshold: float | None = None, label: str = 'unnamed') -> DiscoveryReport: 
2096def auto_discovery(
2097    outcome: Any,
2098    candidate_pool: dict[str, Any],
2099    controls: dict[str, Any],
2100    *,
2101    max_features: int = 20,
2102    min_abs_spearman: float = 0.15,
2103    orthogonal_threshold: float | None = None,
2104    label: str = "unnamed",
2105) -> DiscoveryReport:
2106    """Sweep a candidate pool for effects; the output is a HYPOTHESIS list.
2107
2108    Every candidate that clears the Bonferroni t-gate (derived from
2109    the number of TESTED candidates: ``alpha / n_tested`` two-sided
2110    normal quantile) and a light spearman pre-filter is listed with
2111    its t, its monotone flag and its Bonferroni-adjusted p.  The
2112    report is EXPLORATORY by construction: it never assigns cells,
2113    never names a best feature, and its doctrine note requires
2114    preregistration + the full pipeline before any candidate can be
2115    believed.  Candidates whose |spearman| against the outcome is
2116    below ``min_abs_spearman`` are not tested (and shrink the
2117    Bonferroni family accordingly, with a note).
2118
2119    Args:
2120        outcome: response series.
2121        candidate_pool: EXPLICIT mapping candidate name -> single
2122            column (an auto-scrape of a frame is deliberately not
2123            supported; the caller owns the pool).
2124        controls: mapping control name -> single column (same rules).
2125        max_features: pool-size cap (exploration hygiene); a larger
2126            pool raises.
2127        min_abs_spearman: pre-filter floor on |spearman| vs the
2128            outcome; 0 disables the filter.
2129        orthogonal_threshold: explicit |t| gate; ``None`` derives the
2130            Bonferroni gate from ``alpha / n_tested``.
2131        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
2132
2133    Returns:
2134        :class:`DiscoveryReport` with ``note`` fixed to
2135        :data:`_DISCOVERY_NOTE`.
2136
2137    Raises:
2138        ValueError: if the pool exceeds ``max_features``, is empty,
2139            ``min_abs_spearman`` is negative, a control collides with
2140            a candidate name, or an input is not a single column.
2141
2142    Example::
2143
2144        >>> import numpy as np
2145        >>> import pandas as pd
2146        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
2147        >>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(500)
2148        >>> planted = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(500), index=idx)
2149        >>> null = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(500), index=idx)
2150        >>> out = pd.Series(1.5 * planted + rng.standard_normal(500),
2151        ...                 index=idx)
2152        >>> report = auto_discovery(
2153        ...     out, {"planted": planted, "null": null}, {},
2154        ...     max_features=5, min_abs_spearman=0.0,
2155        ... )
2156        >>> [entry["feature"] for entry in report["discovered"]]
2157        ['planted']
2158        >>> report["all_below_threshold"]
2159        False
2160    """
2161    if not candidate_pool:
2162        raise ValueError("candidate_pool must not be empty")
2163    if len(candidate_pool) > max_features:
2164        raise ValueError(
2165            f"candidate pool size {len(candidate_pool)} exceeds"
2166            f" max_features ({max_features}); the caller must shrink"
2167            " the pool explicitly"
2168        )
2169    if min_abs_spearman < 0.0 or not np.isfinite(min_abs_spearman):
2170        raise ValueError(
2171            f"min_abs_spearman must be a finite float >= 0, got"
2172            f" {min_abs_spearman!r}"
2173        )
2174    candidate_names = list(candidate_pool)
2175    control_names = list(controls)
2176    overlap = sorted(set(candidate_names) & set(control_names))
2177    if overlap:
2178        raise ValueError(f"candidate and control names collide: {overlap}")
2179    outcome_series = _to_series(outcome, "outcome")
2180    control_series = [
2181        _to_series(controls[name], name) for name in control_names
2182    ]
2183    notes: list[str] = []
2184    tested: dict[str, pd.Series] = {}
2185    for name in candidate_names:
2186        candidate_series = _to_series(candidate_pool[name], name)
2187        aligned_out, aligned_feat = align_inputs(
2188            outcome_series, candidate_series
2189        )
2190        rho, rho_p = _spearman_pair(aligned_feat, aligned_out)
2191        if (
2192            min_abs_spearman > 0.0
2193            and np.isfinite(rho)
2194            and abs(rho) < min_abs_spearman
2195        ):
2196            notes.append(
2197                f"{name}: below the spearman floor"
2198                f" (|rho| = {abs(rho):.3f} < {min_abs_spearman}); not"
2199                " tested (shrinks the Bonferroni family)"
2200            )
2201            continue
2202        tested[name] = candidate_series
2203    n_tested = len(tested)
2204    if n_tested == 0:
2205        return DiscoveryReport(
2206            label=label,
2207            n_candidates=0,
2208            t_gate=float("nan"),
2209            discovered=[],
2210            all_below_threshold=True,
2211            note=_DISCOVERY_NOTE,
2212            notes=[
2213                *notes,
2214                "every candidate fell below the spearman floor",
2215            ],
2216        )
2217    if orthogonal_threshold is None:
2218        t_gate = float(norm.isf(_ALPHA / n_tested / 2.0))
2219        notes.append(
2220            f"Bonferroni t-gate from alpha/{n_tested}: |t| >= {t_gate:.3f}"
2221        )
2222    else:
2223        if not np.isfinite(orthogonal_threshold) or (
2224            orthogonal_threshold <= 0
2225        ):
2226            raise ValueError(
2227                "orthogonal_threshold must be a positive finite float,"
2228                f" got {orthogonal_threshold!r}"
2229            )
2230        t_gate = float(orthogonal_threshold)
2231    discovered: list[DiscoveryEntry] = []
2232    for name, candidate_series in tested.items():
2233        aligned = align_inputs(
2234            outcome_series, candidate_series, *control_series
2235        )
2236        aligned_out = aligned[0]
2237        aligned_feat = aligned[1]
2238        design = np.column_stack([np.ones(aligned_out.size), *aligned[1:]])
2239        fit = ols_hc0(aligned_out, design)
2240        t_stat = float(fit["t"][1])
2241        rho, rho_p = _spearman_pair(aligned_feat, aligned_out)
2242        monotone = bool(
2243            np.isfinite(rho) and np.isfinite(rho_p) and rho_p <= _SPEAR_P_GATE
2244        )
2245        if np.isfinite(t_stat) and abs(t_stat) >= t_gate:
2246            p_two_sided = (
2247                2.0 * float(stats.t.sf(abs(t_stat), fit["df"]))
2248                if np.isfinite(t_stat)
2249                else 1.0
2250            )
2251            discovered.append(
2252                DiscoveryEntry(
2253                    feature=name,
2254                    t_stat=t_stat,
2255                    monotone=monotone,
2256                    p_bonferroni=float(min(1.0, p_two_sided * n_tested)),
2257                )
2258            )
2259    return DiscoveryReport(
2260        label=label,
2261        n_candidates=n_tested,
2262        t_gate=t_gate,
2263        discovered=discovered,
2264        all_below_threshold=len(discovered) == 0,
2265        note=_DISCOVERY_NOTE,
2266        notes=notes,
2267    )

Sweep a candidate pool for effects; the output is a HYPOTHESIS list.

Every candidate that clears the Bonferroni t-gate (derived from the number of TESTED candidates: alpha / n_tested two-sided normal quantile) and a light spearman pre-filter is listed with its t, its monotone flag and its Bonferroni-adjusted p. The report is EXPLORATORY by construction: it never assigns cells, never names a best feature, and its doctrine note requires preregistration + the full pipeline before any candidate can be believed. Candidates whose |spearman| against the outcome is below min_abs_spearman are not tested (and shrink the Bonferroni family accordingly, with a note).

Args: outcome: response series. candidate_pool: EXPLICIT mapping candidate name -> single column (an auto-scrape of a frame is deliberately not supported; the caller owns the pool). controls: mapping control name -> single column (same rules). max_features: pool-size cap (exploration hygiene); a larger pool raises. min_abs_spearman: pre-filter floor on |spearman| vs the outcome; 0 disables the filter. orthogonal_threshold: explicit |t| gate; None derives the Bonferroni gate from alpha / n_tested. label: free-text tag stored under report["label"].

Returns: DiscoveryReport with note fixed to _DISCOVERY_NOTE.

Raises: ValueError: if the pool exceeds max_features, is empty, min_abs_spearman is negative, a control collides with a candidate name, or an input is not a single column.

Example::

>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
>>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(500)
>>> planted = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(500), index=idx)
>>> null = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(500), index=idx)
>>> out = pd.Series(1.5 * planted + rng.standard_normal(500),
...                 index=idx)
>>> report = auto_discovery(
...     out, {"planted": planted, "null": null}, {},
...     max_features=5, min_abs_spearman=0.0,
... )
>>> [entry["feature"] for entry in report["discovered"]]
['planted']
>>> report["all_below_threshold"]
False
def auto_rule_generation( outcome: Any, features: dict[str, typing.Any], rule_specs: dict[str, dict[str, typing.Any]], *, max_depth: int = 2, top_k: int = 5, min_n_train_kept: int = 100, train_idx: Any, test_idx: Any, label: str = 'unnamed') -> AutoRuleReport: 
2452def auto_rule_generation(
2453    outcome: Any,
2454    features: dict[str, Any],
2455    rule_specs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
2456    *,
2457    max_depth: int = 2,
2458    top_k: int = 5,
2459    min_n_train_kept: int = 100,
2460    train_idx: Any,
2461    test_idx: Any,
2462    label: str = "unnamed",
2463) -> AutoRuleReport:
2464    """Grid-search rule VALUES on train; the test split judges them.
2465
2466    The caller fixes the rule SHAPE (an AND-of-comparisons template
2467    like ``"feat_a < {t1} & feat_b <= {t2}"`` plus one grid per
2468    clause); the tool enumerates value combinations ON THE TRAIN
2469    SPLIT ONLY, keeps the ``top_k`` by ``delta_train``, and only then
2470    looks at the untouched test split.  Candidates whose
2471    ``delta_test`` is positive land in ``valid_rules``;
2472    ``overfit_warning`` fires when every kept candidate fails on
2473    test.  EXPLORATORY by construction: generation without a frozen
2474    downstream preregistration is exactly the winner's curse the
2475    framework exists to kill.
2476
2477    Args:
2478        outcome: response series WITHOUT NaN.
2479        features: mapping feature name -> single column (every
2480            template feature must be declared here).
2481        rule_specs: ``{spec_name: {template: str, grids:
2482            [[values], ...]}}``; ``len(grids)`` must equal the
2483            template's clause count.
2484        max_depth: clause-count cap (at least 1).
2485        top_k: how many train winners face the test split; at
2486            least 1.
2487        min_n_train_kept: minimum kept rows on train for ``valid``.
2488        train_idx: positional train split.
2489        test_idx: positional test split (must not overlap).
2490        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
2491
2492    Returns:
2493        :class:`AutoRuleReport` with ``candidates`` ordered by
2494        ``delta_train`` (best first).
2495
2496    Raises:
2497        ValueError: on template deviations (see
2498            :func:`_parse_multi_rule_template`), a grid count or
2499            combo count mismatch, an over-cap grid product
2500            (:data:`_MAX_COMBOS`), NaN outcome, or bad splits.
2501
2502    Example::
2503
2504        >>> import numpy as np
2505        >>> import pandas as pd
2506        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
2507        >>> rows = np.arange(600)
2508        >>> feat = pd.Series(rng.uniform(0, 1, 600), index=rows)
2509        >>> out = pd.Series(
2510        ...     np.where(feat < 0.5, 1.0, 0.0)
2511        ...     + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(600), index=rows
2512        ... )
2513        >>> report = auto_rule_generation(
2514        ...     out, {"feat": feat},
2515        ...     {"low": {"template": "feat < {t1}",
2516        ...              "grids": [[0.4, 0.5, 0.6]]}},
2517        ...     min_n_train_kept=30,
2518        ...     train_idx=np.arange(400), test_idx=np.arange(400, 600),
2519        ... )
2520        >>> report["best_valid_rule"] is not None
2521        True
2522        >>> report["overfit_warning"]
2523        False
2524    """
2525    if not rule_specs:
2526        raise ValueError("rule_specs must not be empty")
2527    validate_int("max_depth", max_depth, minimum=1)
2528    validate_int("top_k", top_k, minimum=1)
2529    validate_int("min_n_train_kept", min_n_train_kept, minimum=1)
2530    feature_names = list(features)
2531    notes: list[str] = []
2532    outcome_series = _to_series(outcome, "outcome")
2533    if bool(outcome_series.isna().any()):
2534        raise ValueError(
2535            "outcome contains NaN; align and drop rows before"
2536            " auto_rule_generation"
2537        )
2538    outcome_values = outcome_series.to_numpy(dtype=float)
2539    train_positions = np.asarray(train_idx, dtype=int).reshape(-1)
2540    test_positions = np.asarray(test_idx, dtype=int).reshape(-1)
2541    if train_positions.size == 0 or test_positions.size == 0:
2542        raise ValueError("train_idx and test_idx must both be non-empty")
2543    if set(train_positions.tolist()) & set(test_positions.tolist()):
2544        raise ValueError("train_idx and test_idx overlap")
2545    total = outcome_values.size
2546    for tag, positions in (
2547        ("train_idx", train_positions),
2548        ("test_idx", test_positions),
2549    ):
2550        if positions.min() < 0 or positions.max() >= total:
2551            raise ValueError(
2552                f"{tag} out of range for outcome of {total} rows"
2553            )
2554    feature_columns = {
2555        name: _to_series(features[name], name).to_numpy(dtype=float)
2556        for name in feature_names
2557    }
2558    train_out = outcome_values[train_positions]
2559    train_rows = train_out.size
2560    evaluated: list[tuple[AutoRuleCandidate, str, tuple[float, ...]]] = []
2561    templates: dict[str, str] = {}
2562    for spec_name, spec in rule_specs.items():
2563        template, parsed, grid_lists = _validate_rule_spec(
2564            spec_name, spec, feature_names, max_depth
2565        )
2566        templates[spec_name] = template
2567        evaluated.extend(
2568            _train_combo_entry(
2569                spec_name,
2570                template,
2571                parsed,
2572                combo,
2573                feature_columns=feature_columns,
2574                train_positions=train_positions,
2575                train_out=train_out,
2576                train_rows=train_rows,
2577            )
2578            for combo in product(*grid_lists)
2579        )
2580    finite = [
2581        entry for entry in evaluated if np.isfinite(entry[0]["delta_train"])
2582    ]
2583    if not finite:
2584        return AutoRuleReport(
2585            label=label,
2586            templates=templates,
2587            candidates=[],
2588            valid_rules=[],
2589            best_valid_rule=None,
2590            overfit_warning=True,
2591            notes=[
2592                *notes,
2593                "every grid combo left one train side empty",
2594            ],
2595        )
2596    finite.sort(key=lambda entry: entry[0]["delta_train"], reverse=True)
2597    top_entries = finite[:top_k]
2598    top_candidates = [entry[0] for entry in top_entries]
2599    _judge_test_entries(
2600        top_entries,
2601        templates,
2602        feature_columns,
2603        feature_names,
2604        max_depth,
2605        outcome_values=outcome_values,
2606        test_positions=test_positions,
2607        min_n_train_kept=min_n_train_kept,
2608    )
2609    valid_names = [
2610        candidate["name"]
2611        for candidate in top_candidates
2612        if candidate["status"] == "valid"
2613    ]
2614    best_valid: str | None = None
2615    if valid_names:
2616        by_name = {
2617            candidate["name"]: candidate for candidate in top_candidates
2618        }
2619        best_valid = max(
2620            valid_names, key=lambda name: by_name[name]["delta_test"]
2621        )
2622    overfit_warning = all(
2623        candidate["status"] != "valid" for candidate in top_candidates
2624    )
2625    return AutoRuleReport(
2626        label=label,
2627        templates=templates,
2628        candidates=top_candidates,
2629        valid_rules=valid_names,
2630        best_valid_rule=best_valid,
2631        overfit_warning=overfit_warning,
2632        notes=notes,
2633    )

Grid-search rule VALUES on train; the test split judges them.

The caller fixes the rule SHAPE (an AND-of-comparisons template like "feat_a < {t1} & feat_b <= {t2}" plus one grid per clause); the tool enumerates value combinations ON THE TRAIN SPLIT ONLY, keeps the top_k by delta_train, and only then looks at the untouched test split. Candidates whose delta_test is positive land in valid_rules; overfit_warning fires when every kept candidate fails on test. EXPLORATORY by construction: generation without a frozen downstream preregistration is exactly the winner's curse the framework exists to kill.

Args: outcome: response series WITHOUT NaN. features: mapping feature name -> single column (every template feature must be declared here). rule_specs: {spec_name: {template: str, grids: [[values], ...]}}; len(grids) must equal the template's clause count. max_depth: clause-count cap (at least 1). top_k: how many train winners face the test split; at least 1. min_n_train_kept: minimum kept rows on train for valid. train_idx: positional train split. test_idx: positional test split (must not overlap). label: free-text tag stored under report["label"].

Returns: AutoRuleReport with candidates ordered by delta_train (best first).

Raises: ValueError: on template deviations (see _parse_multi_rule_template()), a grid count or combo count mismatch, an over-cap grid product (_MAX_COMBOS), NaN outcome, or bad splits.

Example::

>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
>>> rows = np.arange(600)
>>> feat = pd.Series(rng.uniform(0, 1, 600), index=rows)
>>> out = pd.Series(
...     np.where(feat < 0.5, 1.0, 0.0)
...     + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(600), index=rows
... )
>>> report = auto_rule_generation(
...     out, {"feat": feat},
...     {"low": {"template": "feat < {t1}",
...              "grids": [[0.4, 0.5, 0.6]]}},
...     min_n_train_kept=30,
...     train_idx=np.arange(400), test_idx=np.arange(400, 600),
... )
>>> report["best_valid_rule"] is not None
True
>>> report["overfit_warning"]
False
def bucket_scan( outcome: Any, features: dict[str, typing.Any], *, n_buckets: int = 5, bucket_edges: dict[str, list[float]] | None = None, min_bucket_n: int = 0, norm_r: typing.Any | None = None, n_perm: int = 200, seed: int = 42, label: str = 'unnamed') -> BucketScanReport: 
1168def bucket_scan(
1169    outcome: Any,
1170    features: dict[str, Any],
1171    *,
1172    n_buckets: int = 5,
1173    bucket_edges: dict[str, list[float]] | None = None,
1174    min_bucket_n: int = 0,
1175    norm_r: Any | None = None,
1176    n_perm: int = 200,
1177    seed: int = 42,
1178    label: str = "unnamed",
1179) -> BucketScanReport:
1180    """Bucket profile, monotonicity and the Q1/Q2 signal split.
1181
1182    For every feature: buckets come from the feature's prereg
1183    ``bucket_edges`` when supplied (else interior quantiles), each
1184    bucket reports n / mean / hit rate / normalized mean / bootstrap
1185    CI, the row-level Spearman gives the monotone verdict (p gate AND
1186    no bucket below ``min_bucket_n``), and a seeded permutation gives
1187    ``p_perm``.  The Q1/Q2 split pools the low and high buckets and
1188    asks where the effect lives: raw outcome (``net_r``), win
1189    frequency (``hit_rate``) or the normalized outcome (``norm_r``).
1190
1191    Args:
1192        outcome: response series.
1193        features: mapping feature name -> single column.
1194        n_buckets: requested bucket count (>= 2).
1195        bucket_edges: optional per-feature interior edges (prereg);
1196            features without an entry fall back to quantiles.
1197        min_bucket_n: power floor per bucket for the monotone
1198            verdict; 0 disables the floor.
1199        norm_r: optional normalized-outcome column (index-aligned
1200            with the outcome; the inner join is performed per
1201            feature); ``None`` uses the outcome itself, in which case
1202            ``norm_r_signal`` mirrors ``net_r_signal`` (Welch t is
1203            invariant to affine scaling -- the report notes this).
1204        n_perm: permutation draws per feature; at least 1.
1205        seed: non-negative seed of the pinned rng.
1206        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
1207
1208    Returns:
1209        :class:`BucketScanReport`; every feature key is present.
1210
1211    Raises:
1212        ValueError: if ``n_buckets`` < 2, ``n_perm`` < 1, ``seed`` is
1213            negative, an input is not a single column, or ``norm_r``
1214            is supplied but does not align with the outcome.
1215
1216    Example::
1217
1218        >>> import numpy as np
1219        >>> import pandas as pd
1220        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
1221        >>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(400)
1222        >>> feat = pd.Series(rng.uniform(0.0, 1.0, 400), index=idx)
1223        >>> out = pd.Series(2.0 * feat + rng.standard_normal(400),
1224        ...                 index=idx)
1225        >>> report = bucket_scan(
1226        ...     out, {"feat": feat}, n_perm=25, seed=42
1227        ... )
1228        >>> report["features"]["feat"]["monotone"]
1229        True
1230    """
1231    validate_int("n_buckets", n_buckets, minimum=2)
1232    validate_int("n_perm", n_perm)
1233    validate_int("seed", seed, minimum=0)
1234    validate_int("min_bucket_n", min_bucket_n, minimum=0)
1235    notes: list[str] = []
1236    outcome_series = _to_series(outcome, "outcome")
1237    norm_is_outcome = norm_r is None
1238    norm_series = (
1239        outcome_series if norm_is_outcome else _to_series(norm_r, "norm_r")
1240    )
1241    entries: dict[str, BucketFeatureReport] = {}
1242    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
1243    for name, feature_value in features.items():
1244        entries[name] = _bucket_profile(
1245            name,
1246            _to_series(feature_value, name),
1247            outcome_series,
1248            norm_series,
1249            n_buckets=n_buckets,
1250            feature_edges=(bucket_edges or {}).get(name),
1251            min_bucket_n=min_bucket_n,
1252            n_perm=n_perm,
1253            rng=rng,
1254            notes=notes,
1255        )
1256    if norm_is_outcome:
1257        notes.append(
1258            "norm_r defaults to the outcome: norm_r_signal mirrors"
1259            " net_r_signal (Welch t is invariant to affine scaling)"
1260        )
1261    return BucketScanReport(
1262        label=label,
1263        n_buckets=n_buckets,
1264        min_bucket_n=min_bucket_n,
1265        norm_r_is_outcome=norm_is_outcome,
1266        features=entries,
1267        notes=notes,
1268    )

Bucket profile, monotonicity and the Q1/Q2 signal split.

For every feature: buckets come from the feature's prereg bucket_edges when supplied (else interior quantiles), each bucket reports n / mean / hit rate / normalized mean / bootstrap CI, the row-level Spearman gives the monotone verdict (p gate AND no bucket below min_bucket_n), and a seeded permutation gives p_perm. The Q1/Q2 split pools the low and high buckets and asks where the effect lives: raw outcome (net_r), win frequency (hit_rate) or the normalized outcome (norm_r).

Args: outcome: response series. features: mapping feature name -> single column. n_buckets: requested bucket count (>= 2). bucket_edges: optional per-feature interior edges (prereg); features without an entry fall back to quantiles. min_bucket_n: power floor per bucket for the monotone verdict; 0 disables the floor. norm_r: optional normalized-outcome column (index-aligned with the outcome; the inner join is performed per feature); None uses the outcome itself, in which case norm_r_signal mirrors net_r_signal (Welch t is invariant to affine scaling -- the report notes this). n_perm: permutation draws per feature; at least 1. seed: non-negative seed of the pinned rng. label: free-text tag stored under report["label"].

Returns: BucketScanReport; every feature key is present.

Raises: ValueError: if n_buckets < 2, n_perm < 1, seed is negative, an input is not a single column, or norm_r is supplied but does not align with the outcome.

Example::

>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
>>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(400)
>>> feat = pd.Series(rng.uniform(0.0, 1.0, 400), index=idx)
>>> out = pd.Series(2.0 * feat + rng.standard_normal(400),
...                 index=idx)
>>> report = bucket_scan(
...     out, {"feat": feat}, n_perm=25, seed=42
... )
>>> report["features"]["feat"]["monotone"]
True
def correlation_cluster( features: dict[str, typing.Any], outcome: Any, *, threshold: float = 0.8, representatives: dict[str, str] | None = None, label: str = 'unnamed') -> ClusterReport: 
 980def correlation_cluster(
 981    features: dict[str, Any],
 982    outcome: Any,
 983    *,
 984    threshold: float = 0.8,
 985    representatives: dict[str, str] | None = None,
 986    label: str = "unnamed",
 987) -> ClusterReport:
 988    """Cluster correlated features; pick one representative each.
 989
 990    Builds the pearson matrix over the aligned complete rows, converts
 991    it to ``1 - |rho|`` distance and cuts an average-linkage tree at
 992    ``threshold``.  The representative of each cluster is the member
 993    with the largest |pearson| against the outcome (insertion order
 994    breaks ties), unless ``representatives`` explicitly pins the
 995    choice: the mapping ``{member: representative}`` must name the
 996    representative and every OTHER member of its cluster (clusters
 997    with no entry auto-pick), point INTO the same cluster, and never
 998    conflict.  ``bonferroni_threshold`` is
 999    ``alpha / n_effective`` -- the family for downstream gates is the
1000    CLUSTER count, not the raw column count.
1001
1002    Args:
1003        features: mapping feature name -> single column.
1004        outcome: response series; only used to rank representatives.
1005        threshold: cut level of |pearson|; in the open (0, 1).
1006        representatives: optional explicit member -> representative
1007            map (validated strictly, see above).
1008        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
1009
1010    Returns:
1011        :class:`ClusterReport` with clusters in stable insertion
1012        order; every member maps to its representative.
1013
1014    Raises:
1015        ValueError: if ``threshold`` is outside (0, 1), ``features``
1016            is empty, no rows survive alignment, a representative
1017            name is unknown, or the explicit map violates the
1018            every-member-or-none / same-cluster / no-conflict rules.
1019
1020    Example::
1021
1022        >>> import numpy as np
1023        >>> import pandas as pd
1024        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
1025        >>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(200)
1026        >>> base = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(200), index=idx)
1027        >>> twin = 0.9 * base + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(200)
1028        >>> lone = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(200), index=idx)
1029        >>> out = pd.Series(base + 0.3 * rng.standard_normal(200),
1030        ...                 index=idx)
1031        >>> report = correlation_cluster(
1032        ...     {"base": base, "twin": twin, "lone": lone}, out
1033        ... )
1034        >>> report["n_effective"]
1035        2
1036        >>> report["representatives"]["twin"]
1037        'base'
1038    """
1039    checked_threshold = _validate_fraction("threshold", threshold)
1040    if not features:
1041        raise ValueError("features dict must not be empty")
1042    names = list(features)
1043    frames = [
1044        _to_series(outcome, "outcome"),
1045        *(_to_series(features[name], name) for name in names),
1046    ]
1047    aligned = pd.concat(frames, axis=1, join="inner").dropna()
1048    if aligned.empty:
1049        raise ValueError("no rows survive alignment; cannot correlate")
1050    notes: list[str] = []
1051    rho_values = aligned[names].corr().to_numpy(dtype=float)
1052    degenerate = [
1053        name
1054        for position, name in enumerate(names)
1055        if not np.isfinite(rho_values[position, position])
1056    ]
1057    notes.extend(
1058        f"{name}: degenerate column (constant or all-NaN after"
1059        " alignment); treated as uncorrelated"
1060        for name in degenerate
1061    )
1062    rho_values = np.where(np.isfinite(rho_values), rho_values, 0.0)
1063    distance_values = 1.0 - np.abs(rho_values)
1064    np.fill_diagonal(distance_values, 0.0)
1065    distance_values = np.clip(
1066        (distance_values + distance_values.T) / 2.0, 0.0, 1.0
1067    )
1068    if len(names) == 1:
1069        labels = np.array([1])
1070    else:
1071        tree = hierarchy.linkage(
1072            squareform(distance_values, checks=False), method="average"
1073        )
1074        labels = hierarchy.fcluster(
1075            tree, t=1.0 - checked_threshold, criterion="distance"
1076        )
1077    groups: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
1078    for name, cluster_id in zip(names, labels, strict=True):
1079        groups.setdefault(int(cluster_id), []).append(name)
1080    order = sorted(groups, key=lambda key: names.index(groups[key][0]))
1081    clusters = [groups[cluster_id] for cluster_id in order]
1082    outcome_values = aligned["outcome"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
1083    rep_map = _resolve_representatives(
1084        clusters, aligned, outcome_values, representatives or {}
1085    )
1086    n_effective = len(clusters)
1087    return ClusterReport(
1088        label=label,
1089        threshold=checked_threshold,
1090        clusters=clusters,
1091        representatives=rep_map,
1092        n_raw=len(names),
1093        n_effective=n_effective,
1094        bonferroni_threshold=_ALPHA / n_effective,
1095        notes=notes,
1096    )

Cluster correlated features; pick one representative each.

Builds the pearson matrix over the aligned complete rows, converts it to 1 - |rho| distance and cuts an average-linkage tree at threshold. The representative of each cluster is the member with the largest |pearson| against the outcome (insertion order breaks ties), unless representatives explicitly pins the choice: the mapping {member: representative} must name the representative and every OTHER member of its cluster (clusters with no entry auto-pick), point INTO the same cluster, and never conflict. bonferroni_threshold is alpha / n_effective -- the family for downstream gates is the CLUSTER count, not the raw column count.

Args: features: mapping feature name -> single column. outcome: response series; only used to rank representatives. threshold: cut level of |pearson|; in the open (0, 1). representatives: optional explicit member -> representative map (validated strictly, see above). label: free-text tag stored under report["label"].

Returns: ClusterReport with clusters in stable insertion order; every member maps to its representative.

Raises: ValueError: if threshold is outside (0, 1), features is empty, no rows survive alignment, a representative name is unknown, or the explicit map violates the every-member-or-none / same-cluster / no-conflict rules.

Example::

>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
>>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(200)
>>> base = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(200), index=idx)
>>> twin = 0.9 * base + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(200)
>>> lone = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(200), index=idx)
>>> out = pd.Series(base + 0.3 * rng.standard_normal(200),
...                 index=idx)
>>> report = correlation_cluster(
...     {"base": base, "twin": twin, "lone": lone}, out
... )
>>> report["n_effective"]
2
>>> report["representatives"]["twin"]
'base'
def feature_analysis( outcome: atropos.data_contract.MaterializedData | pandas.Series, features: dict[str, typing.Any] | pandas.DataFrame | None = None, controls: dict[str, typing.Any] | pandas.DataFrame | None = None, *, nan_threshold: float = 0.05, cluster_threshold: float = 0.8, representatives: dict[str, str] | None = None, orthogonal_threshold: float | None = None, n_perm_orth: int = 200, n_buckets: int = 5, bucket_edges: dict[str, list[float]] | None = None, min_bucket_n: int = 50, norm_r: typing.Any | None = None, n_perm_bucket: int = 200, interaction_pairs: list[tuple[str, str]] | None = None, min_cell_n: int = 30, candidate_rules: dict[str, typing.Any] | None = None, train_idx: typing.Any | None = None, test_idx: typing.Any | None = None, regime_indicator: dict[str, typing.Any] | None = None, min_regime_n: int = 100, threshold_specs: dict[str, list[float]] | None = None, threshold_template: str | None = None, min_n_kept: int = 100, discovery_pool: dict[str, typing.Any] | None = None, discovery_min_abs_spearman: float = 0.15, importance_model: str | None = None, importance_n_permutations: int = 100, rule_generation_specs: dict[str, dict[str, typing.Any]] | None = None, rule_generation_top_k: int = 5, seed: int = 42, label: str = 'unnamed') -> FeatureAnalysisReport: 
3100def feature_analysis(
3101    outcome: MaterializedData | pd.Series,
3102    features: dict[str, Any] | pd.DataFrame | None = None,
3103    controls: dict[str, Any] | pd.DataFrame | None = None,
3104    *,

3106    cluster_threshold: float = 0.8,
3107    representatives: dict[str, str] | None = None,
3108    orthogonal_threshold: float | None = None,
3109    n_perm_orth: int = 200,
3110    n_buckets: int = 5,
3111    bucket_edges: dict[str, list[float]] | None = None,
3112    min_bucket_n: int = 50,
3113    norm_r: Any | None = None,
3114    n_perm_bucket: int = 200,
3115    interaction_pairs: list[tuple[str, str]] | None = None,
3116    min_cell_n: int = 30,
3117    candidate_rules: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
3118    train_idx: Any | None = None,
3119    test_idx: Any | None = None,
3120    regime_indicator: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
3121    min_regime_n: int = 100,
3122    threshold_specs: dict[str, list[float]] | None = None,
3123    threshold_template: str | None = None,
3124    min_n_kept: int = 100,
3125    discovery_pool: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
3126    discovery_min_abs_spearman: float = 0.15,
3127    importance_model: str | None = None,
3128    importance_n_permutations: int = 100,
3129    rule_generation_specs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
3130    rule_generation_top_k: int = 5,
3131    seed: int = 42,
3132    label: str = "unnamed",
3133) -> FeatureAnalysisReport:
3134    """Chain the scans, then classify every representative feature.
3135
3136    Order (each stage feeds the next): missingness flags ->
3137    correlation clusters (Bonferroni family = ``n_effective``) ->
3138    orthogonal check on the REPRESENTATIVES with the derived t-gate
3139    (``alpha / n_effective`` two-sided normal quantile unless
3140    ``orthogonal_threshold`` overrides it) -> bucket scan on the
3141    orthogonally detected features -> interaction scans for the
3142    requested pairs -> rule fit when candidate rules AND a frozen
3143    split are supplied -> regime scan when an indicator is supplied
3144    (on the detected features) -> threshold sweeps when specs are
3145    supplied (requires the frozen split) -> classification ->
3146    recommended actions.
3147
3148    Classification (per representative): not testable -> ``NOISE``;
3149    orthogonal gate fail -> ``PROXY``; pass + non-monotone ->
3150    ``SHAPE_UNKNOWN``; pass + monotone goes through the regime gate:
3151    a VERIFIED indicator (``prereg_hash``, 2+ qualifying regimes)
3152    upgrades monotone-in-every-regime features to ``STRONG`` and
3153    monotone-in-some to ``REGIME_DEPENDENT``; anything weaker stays
3154    ``STRONG_UNVERIFIED``.  Cluster members get no independent cell:
3155    ``skipped_features`` points them at their representative.  The
3156    discovery/importance/rule-generation blocks land in checkpoint
3157    A3 and read ``None`` until then.
3158
3159    Args:
3160        outcome: a :class:`~atropos.data_contract.MaterializedData`
3161            bundle (the contract path -- its manifest is VALIDATED:
3162            a failed lookahead check or a failed validation battery
3163            is fatal, a missing manifest is a loud warning in the
3164            report notes) or the response series (legacy path).
3165        features: mapping feature name -> single column, or a
3166            DataFrame; ``None`` when ``outcome`` is a
3167            MaterializedData (the bundle carries the columns).
3168        controls: mapping control name -> single column, or a
3169            DataFrame; ``None`` when ``outcome`` is a
3170            MaterializedData.
3171        nan_threshold: missingness warn gate; in the open (0, 1).
3172        cluster_threshold: cluster cut level of |pearson|.
3173        representatives: optional explicit member -> representative
3174            map (see :func:`correlation_cluster`).
3175        orthogonal_threshold: explicit |t| gate for the orthogonal
3176            check; ``None`` derives ``alpha / n_effective``.
3177        n_perm_orth: permutation draws for the orthogonal check.
3178        n_buckets: requested bucket count for :func:`bucket_scan`.
3179        bucket_edges: optional per-feature prereg bucket edges.
3180        min_bucket_n: power floor per bucket (0 disables).
3181        norm_r: optional normalized-outcome column (see
3182            :func:`bucket_scan`).
3183        n_perm_bucket: permutation draws per bucket feature.
3184        interaction_pairs: optional list of ``(name_a, name_b)``
3185            pairs to test; both names must be declared features.
3186        min_cell_n: power floor per interaction cell.
3187        candidate_rules: optional rule masks for :func:`rule_fit`;
3188            requires ``train_idx`` AND ``test_idx``.
3189        train_idx: positional train split for ``candidate_rules`` and
3190            the threshold sweeps.
3191        test_idx: positional test split (see ``train_idx``).
3192        regime_indicator: optional ``{name, definition, prereg_hash,
3193            values}`` dict for :func:`regime_scan` (see there); the
3194            gate demands ``prereg_hash`` for a STRONG cell.
3195        min_regime_n: minimum rows per regime for the sign/monotone
3196            comparison.
3197        threshold_specs: optional ``{feature: [thresholds]}`` sweeps
3198            for :func:`threshold_scan`; requires the frozen split.
3199        threshold_template: optional format string with ``{feature}``
3200            and ``{t}`` placeholders (default ``"{feature} < {t}"``).
3201        min_n_kept: minimum kept rows per split for a ``valid``
3202            threshold point.
3203        discovery_pool: optional explicit candidate dict for
3204            :func:`auto_discovery` -- EXPLORATORY output, never
3205            merged into the classification.
3206        discovery_min_abs_spearman: spearman pre-filter floor for
3207            the discovery pool.
3208        importance_model: optional ``"linear"`` / ``"tree"`` for
3209            :func:`feature_importance` -- diagnostic only, feeds no
3210            cell.
3211        importance_n_permutations: permutation repeats for the
3212            importance runs.
3213        rule_generation_specs: optional ``{name: {template, grids}}``
3214            for :func:`auto_rule_generation`; requires the frozen
3215            split.  EXPLORATORY output.
3216        rule_generation_top_k: how many train winners face the test
3217            split.
3218        seed: non-negative seed threaded into every seeded step.
3219        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
3220
3221    Returns:
3222        :class:`FeatureAnalysisReport`; every schema key is present.
3223
3224    Raises:
3225        ValueError: if gate fractions are outside (0, 1), a pair name
3226            is not a declared feature, ``candidate_rules`` is given
3227            without both split indices, ``outcome`` is a
3228            MaterializedData whose manifest fails (lookahead check or
3229            validation battery), ``features``/``controls`` are passed
3230            alongside a MaterializedData, or any sub-scan raises.

3232    Example::
3233
3234        >>> import numpy as np
3235        >>> import pandas as pd
3236        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
3237        >>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(500)
3238        >>> feat = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(500), index=idx)
3239        >>> ctrl = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(500), index=idx)
3240        >>> out = pd.Series(0.5 * feat + rng.standard_normal(500),
3241        ...                 index=idx)

3244        ...     n_perm_orth=25, n_perm_bucket=25, min_bucket_n=0,
3245        ...     label="demo",
3246        ... )
3247        >>> report["classification"]["feat"]
3248        'STRONG_UNVERIFIED'
3249    """
3250    _validate_fraction("nan_threshold", nan_threshold)
3251    _validate_fraction("cluster_threshold", cluster_threshold)
3252    validate_int("seed", seed, minimum=0)
3253    notes: list[str] = []
3254    feature_map, control_map = _resolve_inputs(
3255        outcome, features, controls, notes
3256    )
3257    outcome_series = (
3258        outcome.outcome if isinstance(outcome, MaterializedData) else outcome
3259    )
3260    if candidate_rules is not None and (
3261        train_idx is None or test_idx is None

3263        raise ValueError(
3264            "candidate_rules requires BOTH train_idx and test_idx"
3265            " (rule_fit has no default split)"
3266        )

3269    missing = missingness_scan(

3272        control_map,

3283    rep_features = {
3284        name: feature_map[name]

3289    if orthogonal_threshold is None:

3310        t_threshold=orth_gate,
3311    )
3312    detected = orth["per_feature_detected"]
3313    bucket_targets = [name for name in rep_features if detected.get(name)]
3314    bucket_edges_kept = {
3315        name: edges
3316        for name, edges in (bucket_edges or {}).items()
3317        if name in bucket_targets
3318    }
3319    buckets = bucket_scan(
3320        outcome_series,
3321        {name: feature_map[name] for name in bucket_targets},
3322        n_buckets=n_buckets,
3323        bucket_edges=bucket_edges_kept or None,
3324        min_bucket_n=min_bucket_n,
3325        norm_r=norm_r,
3326        n_perm=n_perm_bucket,
3327        seed=seed,

3329    )

3332    )
3333    rules = None

3336            outcome_series,
3337            candidate_rules,
3338            train_idx=train_idx,
3339            test_idx=test_idx,
3340            label=label,
3341        )
3342    regime = None

3347            regime_indicator,

3349            label=label,
3350        )
3351    threshold_reports = _run_threshold_sweeps(
3352        outcome_series,
3353        feature_map,
3354        threshold_specs,
3355        threshold_template,

3357        test_idx=test_idx,
3358        min_n_kept=min_n_kept,
3359    )
3360    discovery, importance, rule_generation = _run_exploratory_blocks(
3361        outcome_series,

3365        discovery_min_abs_spearman=discovery_min_abs_spearman,
3366        importance_model=importance_model,
3367        importance_n_permutations=importance_n_permutations,
3368        rule_generation_specs=rule_generation_specs,
3369        rule_generation_top_k=rule_generation_top_k,
3370        train_idx=train_idx,

3378    )

3391        orthogonal=orth,
3392        buckets=buckets,
3393        interaction=interactions,

3398        importance=importance,
3399        rule_generation=rule_generation,
3400        skipped_features=skipped,
