3402        recommended_actions=actions,
3403        notes=notes,
3404    )

Chain the scans, then classify every representative feature.

Order (each stage feeds the next): missingness flags -> correlation clusters (Bonferroni family = n_effective) -> orthogonal check on the REPRESENTATIVES with the derived t-gate (alpha / n_effective two-sided normal quantile unless orthogonal_threshold overrides it) -> bucket scan on the orthogonally detected features -> interaction scans for the requested pairs -> rule fit when candidate rules AND a frozen split are supplied -> regime scan when an indicator is supplied (on the detected features) -> threshold sweeps when specs are supplied (requires the frozen split) -> classification -> recommended actions.

Classification (per representative): not testable -> NOISE; orthogonal gate fail -> PROXY; pass + non-monotone -> SHAPE_UNKNOWN; pass + monotone goes through the regime gate: a VERIFIED indicator (prereg_hash, 2+ qualifying regimes) upgrades monotone-in-every-regime features to STRONG and monotone-in-some to REGIME_DEPENDENT; anything weaker stays STRONG_UNVERIFIED. Cluster members get no independent cell: skipped_features points them at their representative. The discovery/importance/rule-generation blocks land in checkpoint A3 and read None until then.

Args: outcome: a ~atropos.data_contract.MaterializedData bundle (the contract path -- its manifest is VALIDATED: a failed lookahead check or a failed validation battery is fatal, a missing manifest is a loud warning in the report notes) or the response series (legacy path). features: mapping feature name -> single column, or a DataFrame; None when outcome is a MaterializedData (the bundle carries the columns). controls: mapping control name -> single column, or a DataFrame; None when outcome is a MaterializedData. nan_threshold: missingness warn gate; in the open (0, 1). cluster_threshold: cluster cut level of |pearson|. representatives: optional explicit member -> representative map (see correlation_cluster()). orthogonal_threshold: explicit |t| gate for the orthogonal check; None derives alpha / n_effective. n_perm_orth: permutation draws for the orthogonal check. n_buckets: requested bucket count for bucket_scan(). bucket_edges: optional per-feature prereg bucket edges. min_bucket_n: power floor per bucket (0 disables). norm_r: optional normalized-outcome column (see bucket_scan()). n_perm_bucket: permutation draws per bucket feature. interaction_pairs: optional list of (name_a, name_b) pairs to test; both names must be declared features. min_cell_n: power floor per interaction cell. candidate_rules: optional rule masks for rule_fit(); requires train_idx AND test_idx. train_idx: positional train split for candidate_rules and the threshold sweeps. test_idx: positional test split (see train_idx). regime_indicator: optional {name, definition, prereg_hash, values} dict for regime_scan() (see there); the gate demands prereg_hash for a STRONG cell. min_regime_n: minimum rows per regime for the sign/monotone comparison. threshold_specs: optional {feature: [thresholds]} sweeps for threshold_scan(); requires the frozen split. threshold_template: optional format string with {feature} and {t} placeholders (default "{feature} < {t}"). min_n_kept: minimum kept rows per split for a valid threshold point. discovery_pool: optional explicit candidate dict for auto_discovery() -- EXPLORATORY output, never merged into the classification. discovery_min_abs_spearman: spearman pre-filter floor for the discovery pool. importance_model: optional "linear" / "tree" for feature_importance() -- diagnostic only, feeds no cell. importance_n_permutations: permutation repeats for the importance runs. rule_generation_specs: optional {name: {template, grids}} for auto_rule_generation(); requires the frozen split. EXPLORATORY output. rule_generation_top_k: how many train winners face the test split. seed: non-negative seed threaded into every seeded step. label: free-text tag stored under report["label"].

Returns: FeatureAnalysisReport; every schema key is present.

Raises: ValueError: if gate fractions are outside (0, 1), a pair name is not a declared feature, candidate_rules is given without both split indices, outcome is a MaterializedData whose manifest fails (lookahead check or validation battery), features/controls are passed alongside a MaterializedData, or any sub-scan raises.

Example::

>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
>>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(500)
>>> feat = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(500), index=idx)
>>> ctrl = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(500), index=idx)
>>> out = pd.Series(0.5 * feat + rng.standard_normal(500),
...                 index=idx)
>>> report = feature_analysis(
...     out, {"feat": feat}, {"ctrl": ctrl},
...     n_perm_orth=25, n_perm_bucket=25, min_bucket_n=0,
...     label="demo",
... )
>>> report["classification"]["feat"]
'STRONG_UNVERIFIED'
def feature_importance( outcome: Any, features: dict[str, typing.Any], *, model: str = 'linear', n_permutations: int = 100, seed: int = 42, label: str = 'unnamed') -> ImportanceReport: 
2273def feature_importance(
2274    outcome: Any,
2275    features: dict[str, Any],
2276    *,
2277    model: str = "linear",
2278    n_permutations: int = 100,
2279    seed: int = 42,
2280    label: str = "unnamed",
2281) -> ImportanceReport:
2282    """Permutation importance of each feature for ONE fitted model.
2283
2284    ``model="linear"`` fits OLS on standardized features;
2285    ``model="tree"`` fits a seeded RandomForest (200 trees, depth 4).
2286    Importance = sklearn permutation importance against R2 with
2287    ``n_repeats=n_permutations``; ``ci_lo`` / ``ci_hi`` are
2288    ``mean +/- 1.96 * std`` of the permutation repeats.  This is a
2289    DIAGNOSTIC: it feeds no classification cell, names no top
2290    feature, and a high importance never rescues a PROXY verdict.
2291
2292    Args:
2293        outcome: response series.
2294        features: mapping feature name -> single column.
2295        model: ``"linear"`` or ``"tree"``.
2296        n_permutations: permutation repeats; at least 1.
2297        seed: non-negative seed for the permutation draws (and the
2298            forest's random_state).
2299        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
2300
2301    Returns:
2302        :class:`ImportanceReport` with one entry per feature.
2303
2304    Raises:
2305        ValueError: if ``model`` is unknown, ``n_permutations`` < 1,
2306            ``seed`` is negative, ``features`` is empty, or fewer
2307            rows than features + 1 survive alignment.
2308
2309    Example::
2310
2311        >>> import numpy as np
2312        >>> import pandas as pd
2313        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
2314        >>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(400)
2315        >>> feat_a = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx)
2316        >>> feat_b = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx)
2317        >>> out = pd.Series(2.0 * feat_a + rng.standard_normal(400),
2318        ...                 index=idx)
2319        >>> report = feature_importance(
2320        ...     out, {"a": feat_a, "b": feat_b}, n_permutations=20
2321        ... )
2322        >>> report["features"]["a"]["importance_mean"] > (
2323        ...     report["features"]["b"]["importance_mean"]
2324        ... )
2325        True
2326    """
2327    if model not in ("linear", "tree"):
2328        raise ValueError(f"model must be 'linear' or 'tree', got {model!r}")
2329    validate_int("n_permutations", n_permutations)
2330    validate_int("seed", seed, minimum=0)
2331    if not features:
2332        raise ValueError("features dict must not be empty")
2333    names = list(features)
2334    aligned = align_inputs(
2335        _to_series(outcome, "outcome"),
2336        *(_to_series(features[name], name) for name in names),
2337    )
2338    outcome_values = aligned[0]
2339    design = np.column_stack(aligned[1:])
2340    n_rows = int(outcome_values.size)
2341    if n_rows <= len(names) + 1:
2342        raise ValueError(
2343            f"too few rows ({n_rows}) for {len(names)} features;"
2344            " importance is undefined"
2345        )
2346    notes: list[str] = []
2347    means = design.mean(axis=0)
2348    stds = design.std(axis=0)
2349    stds[stds == 0.0] = 1.0
2350    design_std = (design - means) / stds
2351    if model == "linear":
2352        fitted = LinearRegression().fit(design_std, outcome_values)
2353    else:
2354        fitted = RandomForestRegressor(
2355            n_estimators=200, max_depth=4, random_state=seed, n_jobs=1
2356        ).fit(design_std, outcome_values)
2357    result = permutation_importance(
2358        fitted,
2359        design_std,
2360        outcome_values,
2361        n_repeats=n_permutations,
2362        random_state=seed,
2363        scoring="r2",
2364    )
2365    entries: dict[str, ImportanceEntry] = {}
2366    for position, name in enumerate(names):
2367        mean_value = float(result.importances_mean[position])
2368        std_value = float(result.importances_std[position])
2369        entries[name] = ImportanceEntry(
2370            importance_mean=mean_value,
2371            importance_std=std_value,
2372            ci_lo=mean_value - 1.96 * std_value,
2373            ci_hi=mean_value + 1.96 * std_value,
2374        )
2375    notes.append(
2376        "diagnostic only: importance feeds no classification cell"
2377        " (see the module docstring)"
2378    )
2379    return ImportanceReport(
2380        label=label,
2381        model=model,
2382        n_permutations=n_permutations,
2383        features=entries,
2384        notes=notes,
2385    )

Permutation importance of each feature for ONE fitted model.

model="linear" fits OLS on standardized features; model="tree" fits a seeded RandomForest (200 trees, depth 4). Importance = sklearn permutation importance against R2 with n_repeats=n_permutations; ci_lo / ci_hi are mean +/- 1.96 * std of the permutation repeats. This is a DIAGNOSTIC: it feeds no classification cell, names no top feature, and a high importance never rescues a PROXY verdict.

Args: outcome: response series. features: mapping feature name -> single column. model: "linear" or "tree". n_permutations: permutation repeats; at least 1. seed: non-negative seed for the permutation draws (and the forest's random_state). label: free-text tag stored under report["label"].

Returns: ImportanceReport with one entry per feature.

Raises: ValueError: if model is unknown, n_permutations < 1, seed is negative, features is empty, or fewer rows than features + 1 survive alignment.

Example::

>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
>>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(400)
>>> feat_a = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx)
>>> feat_b = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx)
>>> out = pd.Series(2.0 * feat_a + rng.standard_normal(400),
...                 index=idx)
>>> report = feature_importance(
...     out, {"a": feat_a, "b": feat_b}, n_permutations=20
... )
>>> report["features"]["a"]["importance_mean"] > (
...     report["features"]["b"]["importance_mean"]
... )
True
def interaction_scan( outcome: Any, feature_a: Any, feature_b: Any, *, n_buckets_a: int = 3, n_buckets_b: int = 4, min_cell_n: int = 30, name_a: str = 'feature_a', name_b: str = 'feature_b', label: str = 'unnamed') -> InteractionScanReport: 
1329def interaction_scan(
1330    outcome: Any,
1331    feature_a: Any,
1332    feature_b: Any,
1333    *,
1334    n_buckets_a: int = 3,
1335    n_buckets_b: int = 4,
1336    min_cell_n: int = 30,
1337    name_a: str = "feature_a",
1338    name_b: str = "feature_b",
1339    label: str = "unnamed",
1340) -> InteractionScanReport:
1341    """Does one pair interact beyond additivity (bucket dummies)?
1342
1343    Quantile-buckets both features, reports the 2-D cell heatmap, then
1344    fits the additive design (intercepts + bucket dummies) and the
1345    full design (plus every dummy product) with OLS and compares them
1346    with the classical nested F-test on the residual sums of squares.
1347    ``interaction_present`` requires the F p-value below
1348    :data:`_ALPHA` AND no cell below ``min_cell_n`` rows -- a
1349    significant F over starved cells is flagged, not claimed.
1350
1351    Args:
1352        outcome: response series.
1353        feature_a: first feature column (heatmap rows).
1354        feature_b: second feature column (heatmap columns).
1355        n_buckets_a: bucket count for ``feature_a`` (>= 2).
1356        n_buckets_b: bucket count for ``feature_b`` (>= 2).
1357        min_cell_n: power floor per cell for the verdict.
1358        name_a: feature name recorded under ``report["feature_a"]``.
1359        name_b: feature name recorded under ``report["feature_b"]``.
1360        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
1361
1362    Returns:
1363        :class:`InteractionScanReport`; ``status`` is ``OK`` or
1364        ``INCONCLUSIVE`` (rank-deficient design, too few rows, or a
1365        degenerate bucket split), with the F statistics NaN in the
1366        latter case.
1367
1368    Raises:
1369        ValueError: if bucket counts are below 2 or an input is not a
1370            single column.
1371
1372    Example::
1373
1374        >>> import numpy as np
1375        >>> import pandas as pd
1376        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
1377        >>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(400)
1378        >>> feat_a = pd.Series(rng.uniform(0, 1, 400), index=idx)
1379        >>> feat_b = pd.Series(rng.uniform(0, 1, 400), index=idx)
1380        >>> out = pd.Series(
1381        ...     feat_a + feat_b + rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx
1382        ... )
1383        >>> report = interaction_scan(out, feat_a, feat_b)
1384        >>> report["interaction_present"]
1385        False
1386    """
1387    validate_int("n_buckets_a", n_buckets_a, minimum=2)
1388    validate_int("n_buckets_b", n_buckets_b, minimum=2)
1389    validate_int("min_cell_n", min_cell_n, minimum=1)
1390    notes: list[str] = []
1391    aligned_out, aligned_a, aligned_b = align_inputs(
1392        _to_series(outcome, "outcome"),
1393        _to_series(feature_a, "feature_a"),
1394        _to_series(feature_b, "feature_b"),
1395    )
1396    ids_a, n_a = _bucket_indices(aligned_a, n_buckets_a, None, notes, name_a)
1397    ids_b, n_b = _bucket_indices(aligned_b, n_buckets_b, None, notes, name_b)
1398    cells: dict[str, InteractionCell] = {}
1399    low_power: list[str] = []
1400    for row_id in range(n_a):
1401        for col_id in range(n_b):
1402            mask = (ids_a == row_id) & (ids_b == col_id)
1403            values = aligned_out[mask]
1404            key = f"{row_id}x{col_id}"
1405            cells[key] = InteractionCell(
1406                n=int(values.size),
1407                mean_outcome=(
1408                    float(np.mean(values)) if values.size else float("nan")
1409                ),
1410                hit_rate=_hit_rate(values),
1411            )
1412            if values.size < min_cell_n:
1413                low_power.append(key)
1414    f_stat, p_f, present, status = _interaction_f_test(
1415        aligned_out,
1416        ids_a,
1417        ids_b,
1418        n_a,
1419        n_b,
1420        low_power=low_power,
1421        notes=notes,
1422    )
1423    if low_power and status == "OK":
1424        notes.append(
1425            f"{len(low_power)} of {len(cells)} cells below min_cell_n"
1426            f" ({min_cell_n}); verdict power-guarded"
1427        )
1428    return InteractionScanReport(
1429        label=label,
1430        feature_a=name_a,
1431        feature_b=name_b,
1432        n_cells=len(cells),
1433        cells=cells,
1434        low_power_cells=low_power,
1435        f_stat=f_stat,
1436        p_f=p_f,
1437        interaction_present=present,
1438        status=status,
1439        notes=notes,
1440    )

Does one pair interact beyond additivity (bucket dummies)?

Quantile-buckets both features, reports the 2-D cell heatmap, then fits the additive design (intercepts + bucket dummies) and the full design (plus every dummy product) with OLS and compares them with the classical nested F-test on the residual sums of squares. interaction_present requires the F p-value below _ALPHA AND no cell below min_cell_n rows -- a significant F over starved cells is flagged, not claimed.

Args: outcome: response series. feature_a: first feature column (heatmap rows). feature_b: second feature column (heatmap columns). n_buckets_a: bucket count for feature_a (>= 2). n_buckets_b: bucket count for feature_b (>= 2). min_cell_n: power floor per cell for the verdict. name_a: feature name recorded under report["feature_a"]. name_b: feature name recorded under report["feature_b"]. label: free-text tag stored under report["label"].

Returns: InteractionScanReport; status is OK or INCONCLUSIVE (rank-deficient design, too few rows, or a degenerate bucket split), with the F statistics NaN in the latter case.

Raises: ValueError: if bucket counts are below 2 or an input is not a single column.

Example::

>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
>>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(400)
>>> feat_a = pd.Series(rng.uniform(0, 1, 400), index=idx)
>>> feat_b = pd.Series(rng.uniform(0, 1, 400), index=idx)
>>> out = pd.Series(
...     feat_a + feat_b + rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx
... )
>>> report = interaction_scan(out, feat_a, feat_b)
>>> report["interaction_present"]
False
def missingness_scan( outcome: Any, features: dict[str, typing.Any], controls: dict[str, typing.Any], *, nan_threshold: float = 0.05, label: str = 'unnamed') -> MissingnessReport: 
815def missingness_scan(
816    outcome: Any,
817    features: dict[str, Any],
818    controls: dict[str, Any],
819    *,
820    nan_threshold: float = 0.05,
821    label: str = "unnamed",
822) -> MissingnessReport:
823    """Is each feature's missingness random, or does it carry signal?
824
825    Works on the UNION index (outer join of outcome, features and
826    controls) -- the rows that a later inner-join alignment would
827    silently drop are exactly the rows this scan must judge.  For
828    every feature: the NaN fraction, a KS test of the outcome where
829    the feature is NaN vs observed, and the pearson correlation of
830    the NaN indicator with every control.  ``warn`` is True only when
831    the fraction exceeds ``nan_threshold`` AND the pattern is
832    non-random (outcome shift or a control link beyond
833    :data:`_NAN_RHO_GATE`) -- random missingness never warns.
834
835    Args:
836        outcome: response series (pandas/numpy 1-D array-like).
837        features: mapping feature name -> single column.
838        controls: mapping control name -> single column.
839        nan_threshold: fraction above which a feature's missingness
840            becomes eligible for the warn flag; in the open (0, 1).
841        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
842
843    Returns:
844        :class:`MissingnessReport`; every key is present for every
845        feature, with NaN statistics where a test was under-powered.
846
847    Raises:
848        ValueError: if ``nan_threshold`` is outside (0, 1), an input
849            is not a single column, or feature/control names collide.
850
851    Example::
852
853        >>> import numpy as np
854        >>> import pandas as pd
855        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
856        >>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(400)
857        >>> out = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx)
858        >>> feat = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx)
859        >>> feat[out > 1.0] = np.nan
860        >>> report = missingness_scan(
861        ...     out, {"feat": feat}, {}, nan_threshold=0.05
862        ... )
863        >>> report["features"]["feat"]["nan_outcome_differs"]
864        True
865    """
866    _validate_fraction("nan_threshold", nan_threshold)
867    feature_names = list(features)
868    control_names = list(controls)
869    overlap = sorted(set(feature_names) & set(control_names))
870    if overlap:
871        raise ValueError(f"feature and control names collide: {overlap}")
872    reserved = sorted((set(feature_names) | set(control_names)) & {"outcome"})
873    if reserved:
874        raise ValueError(
875            "the name 'outcome' is reserved for the outcome column;"
876            f" rename: {reserved}"
877        )
878    outcome_series = _to_series(outcome, "outcome")
879    feature_series = {
880        name: _to_series(features[name], name) for name in feature_names
881    }
882    control_series = {
883        name: _to_series(controls[name], name) for name in control_names
884    }
885    union = pd.concat(
886        [outcome_series, *feature_series.values(), *control_series.values()],
887        axis=1,
888        join="outer",
889    )
890    outcome_values = union["outcome"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
891    entries: dict[str, MissingnessEntry] = {}
892    notes: list[str] = []
893    for name in feature_names:
894        entries[name] = _missingness_entry(
895            name,
896            union[name].to_numpy(dtype=float),
897            outcome_values,
898            union,
899            control_names,
900            nan_threshold=nan_threshold,
901            notes=notes,
902        )
903    return MissingnessReport(
904        label=label,
905        nan_threshold=nan_threshold,
906        features=entries,
907        notes=notes,
908    )

Is each feature's missingness random, or does it carry signal?

Works on the UNION index (outer join of outcome, features and controls) -- the rows that a later inner-join alignment would silently drop are exactly the rows this scan must judge. For every feature: the NaN fraction, a KS test of the outcome where the feature is NaN vs observed, and the pearson correlation of the NaN indicator with every control. warn is True only when the fraction exceeds nan_threshold AND the pattern is non-random (outcome shift or a control link beyond _NAN_RHO_GATE) -- random missingness never warns.

Args: outcome: response series (pandas/numpy 1-D array-like). features: mapping feature name -> single column. controls: mapping control name -> single column. nan_threshold: fraction above which a feature's missingness becomes eligible for the warn flag; in the open (0, 1). label: free-text tag stored under report["label"].

Returns: MissingnessReport; every key is present for every feature, with NaN statistics where a test was under-powered.

Raises: ValueError: if nan_threshold is outside (0, 1), an input is not a single column, or feature/control names collide.

Example::

>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
>>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(400)
>>> out = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx)
>>> feat = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx)
>>> feat[out > 1.0] = np.nan
>>> report = missingness_scan(
...     out, {"feat": feat}, {}, nan_threshold=0.05
... )
>>> report["features"]["feat"]["nan_outcome_differs"]
True
def regime_scan( outcome: Any, features: dict[str, typing.Any], regime_indicator: dict[str, typing.Any], *, min_regime_n: int = 100, label: str = 'unnamed') -> RegimeScanReport: 
1706def regime_scan(
1707    outcome: Any,
1708    features: dict[str, Any],
1709    regime_indicator: dict[str, Any],
1710    *,
1711    min_regime_n: int = 100,
1712    label: str = "unnamed",
1713) -> RegimeScanReport:
1714    """Is a feature's effect regime-stable, or does the sign flip?
1715
1716    Splits the aligned sample by the caller's regime indicator (a
1717    dict carrying ``name``, ``definition``, ``prereg_hash`` and the
1718    ``values`` Series) and profiles every feature inside every regime
1719    value: n, row-level Spearman, and the monotone verdict.  The
1720    indicator MUST be preregistered (``prereg_hash``): an unfrozen
1721    indicator reads ``REGIME_UNVERIFIED`` -- cells are computed but
1722    can never upgrade a classification to STRONG.  Regimes with fewer
1723    than ``min_regime_n`` rows are excluded from the sign comparison
1724    with a note.
1725
1726    Args:
1727        outcome: response series.
1728        features: mapping feature name -> single column.
1729        regime_indicator: ``{name, definition, prereg_hash, values}``;
1730            ``values`` is the regime Series (labels may be numeric or
1731            string), index-aligned with the outcome.
1732        min_regime_n: minimum rows for a regime to qualify for the
1733            sign comparison; at least 1.
1734        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
1735
1736    Returns:
1737        :class:`RegimeScanReport`; ``same_sign[feature]`` is the
1738        pairwise sign test over qualifying regimes, ``strongest_regime``
1739        / ``weakest_regime`` name the regimes by |spearman|.
1740
1741    Raises:
1742        ValueError: if the indicator dict misses a key, has an empty
1743            name/definition, ``min_regime_n`` < 1, or an input is not
1744            a single column.
1745
1746    Example::
1747
1748        >>> import numpy as np
1749        >>> import pandas as pd
1750        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
1751        >>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(400)
1752        >>> feat = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx)
1753        >>> out = pd.Series(2.0 * feat + rng.standard_normal(400),
1754        ...                 index=idx)
1755        >>> regime = pd.Series(np.where(rng.random(400) < 0.5, 0, 1),
1756        ...                    index=idx)
1757        >>> report = regime_scan(
1758        ...     out, {"feat": feat},
1759        ...     {"name": "coin", "definition": "independent coin",
1760        ...      "prereg_hash": "hash", "values": regime},
1761        ...     min_regime_n=50,
1762        ... )
1763        >>> report["same_sign"]["feat"]
1764        True
1765    """
1766    for key in ("name", "definition", "prereg_hash", "values"):
1767        if key not in regime_indicator:
1768            raise ValueError(
1769                f"regime_indicator must carry {key!r}; got keys"
1770                f" {sorted(regime_indicator)}"
1771            )
1772    if not regime_indicator["name"] or not regime_indicator["definition"]:
1773        raise ValueError(
1774            "regime_indicator name and definition must be non-empty"
1775        )
1776    validate_int("min_regime_n", min_regime_n, minimum=1)
1777    prereg_hash = regime_indicator["prereg_hash"]
1778    notes: list[str] = []
1779    if prereg_hash:
1780        status = "OK"
1781    else:
1782        status = "REGIME_UNVERIFIED"
1783        notes.append(
1784            "regime indicator carries no prereg_hash: status"
1785            " REGIME_UNVERIFIED -- cells can never upgrade a"
1786            " classification to STRONG"
1787        )
1788    outcome_series = _to_series(outcome, "outcome")
1789    values_series = _to_raw_series(regime_indicator["values"], "regime_value")
1790    entries: dict[str, dict[str, RegimeEntry]] = {}
1791    same_sign: dict[str, bool] = {}
1792    strongest_regime: dict[str, str] = {}
1793    weakest_regime: dict[str, str] = {}
1794    for name, feature_value in features.items():
1795        feature_series = _to_series(feature_value, name)
1796        frame = pd.concat(
1797            [outcome_series, feature_series, values_series],
1798            axis=1,
1799            join="inner",
1800        ).dropna()
1801        aligned_out = frame["outcome"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
1802        aligned_feat = frame[name].to_numpy(dtype=float)
1803        labels = frame["regime_value"].to_numpy()
1804        feature_entries: dict[str, RegimeEntry] = {}
1805        for label_value in sorted(set(labels.tolist()), key=str):
1806            mask = labels == label_value
1807            slice_rho, slice_p = _spearman_pair(
1808                aligned_feat[mask], aligned_out[mask]
1809            )
1810            feature_entries[str(label_value)] = RegimeEntry(
1811                n=int(mask.sum()),
1812                spearman=slice_rho,
1813                spearman_p=slice_p,
1814                monotone=bool(
1815                    np.isfinite(slice_rho)
1816                    and np.isfinite(slice_p)
1817                    and slice_p <= _SPEAR_P_GATE
1818                ),
1819            )
1820        qualifying = [
1821            regime_key
1822            for regime_key, entry in feature_entries.items()
1823            if entry["n"] >= min_regime_n
1824        ]
1825        excluded = [
1826            regime_key
1827            for regime_key, entry in feature_entries.items()
1828            if entry["n"] < min_regime_n
1829        ]
1830        if excluded:
1831            notes.append(
1832                f"{name}: regimes excluded from the sign comparison"
1833                f" (below min_regime_n = {min_regime_n}): {excluded}"
1834            )
1835        if len(qualifying) < 2:
1836            notes.append(
1837                f"{name}: fewer than 2 qualifying regimes; same_sign"
1838                " reads False (not testable, not a flip)"
1839            )
1840            same_sign[name] = False
1841            strongest_regime[name] = ""
1842            weakest_regime[name] = ""
1843        else:
1844            rhos = {
1845                regime_key: feature_entries[regime_key]["spearman"]
1846                for regime_key in qualifying
1847            }
1848            signs = {
1849                np.sign(value)
1850                for value in rhos.values()
1851                if np.isfinite(value)
1852            }
1853            same_sign[name] = bool(len(signs) == 1 and signs)
1854            strongest_regime[name] = max(
1855                qualifying, key=lambda key: abs(rhos[key])
1856            )
1857            weakest_regime[name] = min(
1858                qualifying, key=lambda key: abs(rhos[key])
1859            )
1860        entries[name] = feature_entries
1861    return RegimeScanReport(
1862        label=label,
1863        regime_name=str(regime_indicator["name"]),
1864        regime_definition=str(regime_indicator["definition"]),
1865        prereg_hash=prereg_hash if prereg_hash else None,
1866        status=status,
1867        min_regime_n=min_regime_n,
1868        features=entries,
1869        same_sign=same_sign,
1870        strongest_regime=strongest_regime,
1871        weakest_regime=weakest_regime,
1872        notes=notes,
1873    )

Is a feature's effect regime-stable, or does the sign flip?

Splits the aligned sample by the caller's regime indicator (a dict carrying name, definition, prereg_hash and the values Series) and profiles every feature inside every regime value: n, row-level Spearman, and the monotone verdict. The indicator MUST be preregistered (prereg_hash): an unfrozen indicator reads REGIME_UNVERIFIED -- cells are computed but can never upgrade a classification to STRONG. Regimes with fewer than min_regime_n rows are excluded from the sign comparison with a note.

Args: outcome: response series. features: mapping feature name -> single column. regime_indicator: {name, definition, prereg_hash, values}; values is the regime Series (labels may be numeric or string), index-aligned with the outcome. min_regime_n: minimum rows for a regime to qualify for the sign comparison; at least 1. label: free-text tag stored under report["label"].

Returns: RegimeScanReport; same_sign[feature] is the pairwise sign test over qualifying regimes, strongest_regime / weakest_regime name the regimes by |spearman|.

Raises: ValueError: if the indicator dict misses a key, has an empty name/definition, min_regime_n < 1, or an input is not a single column.

Example::

>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
>>> idx = pd.RangeIndex(400)
>>> feat = pd.Series(rng.standard_normal(400), index=idx)
>>> out = pd.Series(2.0 * feat + rng.standard_normal(400),
...                 index=idx)
>>> regime = pd.Series(np.where(rng.random(400) < 0.5, 0, 1),
...                    index=idx)
>>> report = regime_scan(
...     out, {"feat": feat},
...     {"name": "coin", "definition": "independent coin",
...      "prereg_hash": "hash", "values": regime},
...     min_regime_n=50,
... )
>>> report["same_sign"]["feat"]
True
def rule_fit( outcome: Any, rules: dict[str, typing.Any], *, train_idx: Any, test_idx: Any, min_n_train: int = 100, min_n_test: int = 50, label: str = 'unnamed') -> RuleFitReport: 
1519def rule_fit(
1520    outcome: Any,
1521    rules: dict[str, Any],
1522    *,
1523    train_idx: Any,
1524    test_idx: Any,
1525    min_n_train: int = 100,
1526    min_n_test: int = 50,
1527    label: str = "unnamed",
1528) -> RuleFitReport:
1529    """Evaluate caller-built rule masks on a frozen train/test split.
1530
1531    For every rule (a boolean mask over the outcome positions) the
1532    kept-minus-dropped outcome mean is computed on the train indices
1533    and on the test indices.  ``status`` applies the sample-size
1534    guards first (``insufficient_n``), then reads the deltas: both
1535    positive -> ``valid``, anything else -> ``unstable`` (a rule that
1536    works on train but not on test lands here -- the honest overfit
1537    signature).  ``best_valid_rule`` names the valid rule with the
1538    largest ``delta_test``, or ``None`` when no rule is valid.
1539
1540    Args:
1541        outcome: response series WITHOUT NaN (NaN rows would corrupt
1542            the positional mask semantics; align and drop first).
1543        rules: mapping rule name -> boolean mask (Series or array)
1544            over the outcome positions.
1545        train_idx: positional indices of the train split.
1546        test_idx: positional indices of the test split; must not
1547            overlap ``train_idx``.
1548        min_n_train: minimum kept rows on train for ``valid``.
1549        min_n_test: minimum kept rows on test for ``valid``.
1550        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
1551
1552    Returns:
1553        :class:`RuleFitReport` with one entry per rule.
1554
1555    Raises:
1556        ValueError: if ``outcome`` contains NaN, the splits are empty
1557            or overlapping, an index is out of range, a mask's length
1558            differs from the outcome, or ``rules`` is empty.
1559
1560    Example::
1561
1562        >>> import numpy as np
1563        >>> import pandas as pd
1564        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
1565        >>> rows = np.arange(300)
1566        >>> out = pd.Series(
1567        ...     np.where(rows % 2 == 0, -1.0, 1.0)
1568        ...     + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(300)
1569        ... )
1570        >>> rule = rows % 2 == 0
1571        >>> report = rule_fit(
1572        ...     out, {"parity": rule},
1573        ...     train_idx=np.arange(200), test_idx=np.arange(200, 300),
1574        ...     min_n_train=10, min_n_test=5,
1575        ... )
1576        >>> report["rules"]["parity"]["status"]
1577        'unstable'
1578    """
1579    validate_int("min_n_train", min_n_train, minimum=1)
1580    validate_int("min_n_test", min_n_test, minimum=1)
1581    if not rules:
1582        raise ValueError("rules dict must not be empty")
1583    outcome_series = _to_series(outcome, "outcome")
1584    if bool(outcome_series.isna().any()):
1585        raise ValueError(
1586            "outcome contains NaN; align and drop rows before rule_fit"
1587        )
1588    outcome_values = outcome_series.to_numpy(dtype=float)
1589    train_positions = np.asarray(train_idx, dtype=int).reshape(-1)
1590    test_positions = np.asarray(test_idx, dtype=int).reshape(-1)
1591    if train_positions.size == 0 or test_positions.size == 0:
1592        raise ValueError("train_idx and test_idx must both be non-empty")
1593    if set(train_positions.tolist()) & set(test_positions.tolist()):
1594        raise ValueError("train_idx and test_idx overlap")
1595    total = outcome_values.size
1596    splits = (
1597        ("train_idx", train_positions),
1598        ("test_idx", test_positions),
1599    )
1600    for tag, positions in splits:
1601        if positions.min() < 0 or positions.max() >= total:
1602            raise ValueError(
1603                f"{tag} out of range for outcome of {total} rows"
1604            )
1605    entries: dict[str, RuleFitEntry] = {}
1606    notes: list[str] = []
1607    for name, mask_value in rules.items():
1608        entries[name] = _rule_entry(
1609            name,
1610            mask_value,
1611            outcome_values,
1612            train_positions,
1613            test_positions,
1614            min_n_train=min_n_train,
1615            min_n_test=min_n_test,
1616            notes=notes,
1617        )
1618    valid_names = [
1619        name
1620        for name, entry in entries.items()
1621        if entry["status"] == _STATUS_VALID
1622    ]
1623    best_valid: str | None = None
1624    if valid_names:
1625        best_valid = max(
1626            valid_names, key=lambda name: entries[name]["delta_test"]
1627        )
1628    return RuleFitReport(
1629        label=label,
1630        rules=entries,
1631        best_valid_rule=best_valid,
1632        notes=notes,
1633    )

Evaluate caller-built rule masks on a frozen train/test split.

For every rule (a boolean mask over the outcome positions) the kept-minus-dropped outcome mean is computed on the train indices and on the test indices. status applies the sample-size guards first (insufficient_n), then reads the deltas: both positive -> valid, anything else -> unstable (a rule that works on train but not on test lands here -- the honest overfit signature). best_valid_rule names the valid rule with the largest delta_test, or None when no rule is valid.

Args: outcome: response series WITHOUT NaN (NaN rows would corrupt the positional mask semantics; align and drop first). rules: mapping rule name -> boolean mask (Series or array) over the outcome positions. train_idx: positional indices of the train split. test_idx: positional indices of the test split; must not overlap train_idx. min_n_train: minimum kept rows on train for valid. min_n_test: minimum kept rows on test for valid. label: free-text tag stored under report["label"].

Returns: RuleFitReport with one entry per rule.

Raises: ValueError: if outcome contains NaN, the splits are empty or overlapping, an index is out of range, a mask's length differs from the outcome, or rules is empty.

Example::

>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
>>> rows = np.arange(300)
>>> out = pd.Series(
...     np.where(rows % 2 == 0, -1.0, 1.0)
...     + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(300)
... )
>>> rule = rows % 2 == 0
>>> report = rule_fit(
...     out, {"parity": rule},
...     train_idx=np.arange(200), test_idx=np.arange(200, 300),
...     min_n_train=10, min_n_test=5,
... )
>>> report["rules"]["parity"]["status"]
'unstable'
def threshold_scan( outcome: Any, feature: Any, rule_template: str, threshold_values: list[float], *, feature_name: str, train_idx: Any, test_idx: Any, min_n_kept: int = 100, label: str = 'unnamed') -> ThresholdScanReport: 
1915def threshold_scan(
1916    outcome: Any,
1917    feature: Any,
1918    rule_template: str,
1919    threshold_values: list[float],
1920    *,
1921    feature_name: str,
1922    train_idx: Any,
1923    test_idx: Any,
1924    min_n_kept: int = 100,
1925    label: str = "unnamed",
1926) -> ThresholdScanReport:
1927    """Sweep one threshold over a fixed rule shape, train then test.
1928
1929    The template pins the shape (``"<feature> <op> {t}"``, parsed,
1930    never evaluated); each threshold builds the rule mask on the
1931    aligned sample and reuses the :func:`rule_fit` ladder
1932    (``min_n_kept`` floors both splits).  The sweep-level reading:
1933    ``plateau_detected`` when both edge deltas hold
1934    :data:`_PLATEAU_SHARE` of the best ``delta_test`` (a wide ridge,
1935    safe to ship), ``edge_detected`` when an edge falls below
1936    :data:`_EDGE_SHARE` of it (a spike -- the pick-one-number
1937    overfit signature), and ``optimal_range`` the contiguous
1938    >= share run around the argmax.
1939
1940    Args:
1941        outcome: response series WITHOUT NaN (aligned with feature).
1942        feature: the feature column the template compares against.
1943        rule_template: format string ``"<feature> <op> {t}"``.
1944        threshold_values: the preregistered thresholds; at most
1945            :data:`_MAX_THRESHOLDS`, at least 2.
1946        feature_name: the feature's declared name (validated against
1947            the template's feature token).
1948        train_idx: positional train split.
1949        test_idx: positional test split (must not overlap train).
1950        min_n_kept: minimum kept rows per split for ``valid``.
1951        label: free-text tag stored under ``report["label"]``.
1952
1953    Returns:
1954        :class:`ThresholdScanReport` with one point per threshold.
1955
1956    Raises:
1957        ValueError: on template deviations (see
1958            :func:`_parse_rule_template`), a sweep outside
1959            [2, _MAX_THRESHOLDS], NaN outcome, or bad splits (the
1960            :func:`rule_fit` guards).
1961
1962    Example::
1963
1964        >>> import numpy as np
1965        >>> import pandas as pd
1966        >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
1967        >>> rows = np.arange(600)
1968        >>> feat = pd.Series(rng.uniform(0, 1, 600), index=rows)
1969        >>> out = pd.Series(
1970        ...     np.where(feat < 0.65, 1.0, 0.0)
1971        ...     + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(600), index=rows
1972        ... )
1973        >>> report = threshold_scan(
1974        ...     out, feat, "feat < {t}",
1975        ...     [0.7, 0.75, 0.8, 0.85, 0.9],
1976        ...     feature_name="feat",
1977        ...     train_idx=np.arange(400), test_idx=np.arange(400, 600),
1978        ...     min_n_kept=30,
1979        ... )
1980        >>> report["plateau_detected"], report["edge_detected"]
1981        (True, False)
1982    """
1983    op, op_func = _parse_rule_template(rule_template, feature_name)
1984    if len(threshold_values) > _MAX_THRESHOLDS:
1985        raise ValueError(
1986            f"threshold sweep length {len(threshold_values)} exceeds"
1987            f" the prereg cap {_MAX_THRESHOLDS}; freeze fewer values"
1988        )
1989    if len(threshold_values) < 2:
1990        raise ValueError(
1991            "threshold sweep needs at least 2 values to read plateau/edge"
1992        )
1993    validate_int("min_n_kept", min_n_kept, minimum=1)
1994    notes: list[str] = []
1995    outcome_series = _to_series(outcome, "outcome")
1996    feature_series = _to_series(feature, feature_name)
1997    frame = pd.concat(
1998        [outcome_series, feature_series], axis=1, join="inner"
1999    ).dropna()
2000    aligned_out = frame["outcome"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
2001    aligned_feat = frame[feature_name].to_numpy(dtype=float)
2002    train_positions = np.asarray(train_idx, dtype=int).reshape(-1)
2003    test_positions = np.asarray(test_idx, dtype=int).reshape(-1)
2004    points: list[ThresholdPoint] = []
2005    for value in threshold_values:
2006        mask = op_func(aligned_feat, float(value))
2007        rule_str = rule_template.format(t=repr(float(value)))
2008        entry = _rule_entry(
2009            rule_str,
2010            mask,
2011            aligned_out,
2012            train_positions,
2013            test_positions,
2014            min_n_train=min_n_kept,
2015            min_n_test=min_n_kept,
2016            notes=notes,
2017        )
2018        points.append(
2019            ThresholdPoint(
2020                threshold=float(value),
2021                rule_str=rule_str,
2022                n_train_kept=entry["n_train_kept"],
2023                n_test_kept=entry["n_test_kept"],
2024                delta_train=entry["delta_train"],
2025                delta_test=entry["delta_test"],
2026                status=entry["status"],
2027            )
2028        )
2029    finite_deltas = [
2030        point["delta_test"]
2031        for point in points
2032        if np.isfinite(point["delta_test"])
2033    ]
2034    plateau = False
2035    edge = False
2036    optimal_range: list[float] | None = None
2037    if len(finite_deltas) < 2:
2038        notes.append(
2039            "fewer than 2 points have a finite delta_test;"
2040            " plateau/edge read False (not testable)"
2041        )
2042    else:
2043        max_delta = max(finite_deltas)
2044        if max_delta <= 0:
2045            notes.append(
2046                "no positive delta_test on the sweep; plateau/edge"
2047                " read False (the rule shape itself fails on test)"
2048            )
2049        else:
2050            first_delta = finite_deltas[0]
2051            last_delta = finite_deltas[-1]
2052            plateau = bool(
2053                first_delta >= _PLATEAU_SHARE * max_delta
2054                and last_delta >= _PLATEAU_SHARE * max_delta
2055            )
2056            edge = bool(
2057                first_delta < _EDGE_SHARE * max_delta
2058                or last_delta < _EDGE_SHARE * max_delta
2059            )
2060            best_pos = finite_deltas.index(max_delta)
2061            low_pos = best_pos
2062            while (
2063                low_pos > 0
2064                and finite_deltas[low_pos - 1] >= _PLATEAU_SHARE * max_delta
2065            ):
2066                low_pos -= 1
2067            high_pos = best_pos
2068            while (
2069                high_pos < len(finite_deltas) - 1
2070                and finite_deltas[high_pos + 1] >= _PLATEAU_SHARE * max_delta
2071            ):
2072                high_pos += 1
2073            finite_points = [
2074                point for point in points if np.isfinite(point["delta_test"])
2075            ]
2076            optimal_range = [
2077                finite_points[low_pos]["threshold"],
2078                finite_points[high_pos]["threshold"],
2079            ]
2080    return ThresholdScanReport(
2081        label=label,
2082        feature=feature_name,
2083        op=op,
2084        rule_template=rule_template,
2085        points=points,
2086        plateau_detected=plateau,
2087        edge_detected=edge,
2088        optimal_range=optimal_range,
2089        notes=notes,
2090    )

Sweep one threshold over a fixed rule shape, train then test.

The template pins the shape ("<feature> <op> {t}", parsed, never evaluated); each threshold builds the rule mask on the aligned sample and reuses the rule_fit() ladder (min_n_kept floors both splits). The sweep-level reading: plateau_detected when both edge deltas hold _PLATEAU_SHARE of the best delta_test (a wide ridge, safe to ship), edge_detected when an edge falls below _EDGE_SHARE of it (a spike -- the pick-one-number overfit signature), and optimal_range the contiguous

= share run around the argmax.

Args: outcome: response series WITHOUT NaN (aligned with feature). feature: the feature column the template compares against. rule_template: format string "<feature> <op> {t}". threshold_values: the preregistered thresholds; at most _MAX_THRESHOLDS, at least 2. feature_name: the feature's declared name (validated against the template's feature token). train_idx: positional train split. test_idx: positional test split (must not overlap train). min_n_kept: minimum kept rows per split for valid. label: free-text tag stored under report["label"].

Returns: ThresholdScanReport with one point per threshold.

Raises: ValueError: on template deviations (see _parse_rule_template()), a sweep outside [2, _MAX_THRESHOLDS], NaN outcome, or bad splits (the rule_fit() guards).

Example::

>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
>>> rows = np.arange(600)
>>> feat = pd.Series(rng.uniform(0, 1, 600), index=rows)
>>> out = pd.Series(
...     np.where(feat < 0.65, 1.0, 0.0)
...     + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(600), index=rows
... )
>>> report = threshold_scan(
...     out, feat, "feat < {t}",
...     [0.7, 0.75, 0.8, 0.85, 0.9],
...     feature_name="feat",
...     train_idx=np.arange(400), test_idx=np.arange(400, 600),
...     min_n_kept=30,
... )
>>> report["plateau_detected"], report["edge_detected"]
(True, False)
